definition_zh: 空的；空虚的；空白；空；无效的；使无效；排泄；虚空
definition_en: empty, lacking something, of no legal force; to make something invalid
core_image: 一只被清空、什么也没留下的容器
scene: 装修工人把旧屋子里的东西全搬走，屋里只剩四面空墙。The workers moved everything out and left a void room behind.
sceneCN: 这里 void 是「空的」（第 1 个义项：里面什么都没有）；句意：工人把所有东西搬走，留下一个空荡荡的房间。

derivatives.zh: 由 void 加名词后缀 -ance 构成，义为「排泄；作废；空缺」
由 void 加过去分词后缀 -ed 构成，义为「已作废的；已被取消的」
源自同一拉丁词根 vacuus，义为「空虚；空白」，与 void 同源但拼写不同
源自同一拉丁词根 vacuus，义为「空洞的；缺乏内容的」

senses.title: Empty of content
senses.definition: containing nothing, or empty of people and things
senses.definitionCN: 里面什么都没有，或人事物都已清空
senses.example: They painted the walls of an empty room, still a void space.
senses.exampleCN: 他们给一间空屋的墙壁上漆，那里仍是一片空荡。
senses.why: The Latin adjective vacuus means empty, and the emptied container is the plainest image of the word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语形容词 vacuus 意为「空的」，被清空容器正是这个词最朴素的画面。

senses.title: A gap left by loss
senses.definition: a deep feeling of emptiness left when someone or something important is gone
senses.definitionCN: 重要的人或事物离开后留下的深深空虚
senses.example: His death left a void that no one could fill.
senses.exampleCN: 他的离世留下了一个无人能填补的空位。
senses.why: If a thing is emptied, the hollow where it stood becomes a felt absence, and emotion fills the space.
senses.whyCN: 事物被清空后，它原来占据的地方就变成可感知的缺席，情感填进了这个空间。

senses.title: Of no legal force
senses.definition: not valid in law, so that an agreement or decision has no effect
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上不成立，协议或决定因此没有效力
senses.example: The contract was declared void after the deal collapsed.
senses.exampleCN: 交易失败后，合同被宣布无效。
senses.why: A contract with nothing in it binds nothing, so the empty image grew into the legal sense of no force.
senses.whyCN: 空无一物的合同约束不了任何人，于是「空」的意象延伸为法律上「没有效力」。

senses.title: Lacking a quality
senses.definition: completely without a particular quality, feeling, or good feature
senses.definitionCN: 完全没有某种品质、感情或优点
senses.example: The plan was void of any clear purpose.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划完全没有明确的目标。
senses.why: The same emptiness can be applied to abstract things, using the pattern void of something.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「空」可以套用到抽象事物上，构成 void of something 这一固定结构。

senses.title: To make invalid
senses.definition: to cancel something so that it no longer has legal or official effect
senses.definitionCN: 取消某事物，使其不再具有法律或官方效力
senses.example: The judge voided the earlier decision.
senses.exampleCN: 法官宣告先前的裁定无效。
senses.why: To void something is to empty it of force, turning the adjective of emptiness into an action.
senses.whyCN: void 作动词就是把某物的效力「掏空」，让形容「空」的词变成动作。

senses.title: To send out waste
senses.definition: to pass urine or other body waste out of the body
senses.definitionCN: 把尿液或其他废物排出体外
senses.example: The patient could not void the bladder after surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 手术之后，患者无法排空膀胱。
senses.why: The medical sense keeps the image of emptying a container, now applied to the body.
senses.whyCN: 医学义保留了「清空容器」的意象，只是换成了身体这个容器。

senses.title: The empty space of the universe
senses.definition: the deep empty space of the universe or of a place
senses.definitionCN: 宇宙或某处深广而空无一物的空间
senses.example: The stars seemed to hang in a vast void.
senses.exampleCN: 星星仿佛悬在一片浩瀚的虚空之中。
senses.why: Literary use stretches the emptied container into the whole dark space beyond the stars.
senses.whyCN: 文学用法把被清空的容器扩大到星辰之外的整片黑暗空间。

intro.en: Void comes through Old French voide, vuide from Latin vacuus, empty, related to vacare, to be empty.
intro.cn: void 经古法语 voide、vuide 而来，出自拉丁语 vacuus（空的），与 vacare（空着）同源。

items.en: Vacuus means empty or vacant, and vacare means to be empty.
items.cn: vacuus 意为「空的」，vacare 意为「空着」。

items.en: Voide and vuide carry the sense of empty into French.
items.cn: voide 与 vuide 把「空」的意思带入法语。

items.en: Old French forms of the word reach English as voide, describing empty space.
items.cn: 该词在十三世纪进入英语，写作 voide，表示空的地方。

items.en: Lawyers begin to use the word for agreements with no force.
items.cn: 法律人士开始用它表示没有效力的协议。

items.en: The verb appears in the sense of emptying or draining something.
items.cn: 动词形式出现，表示排空、排出某物。

items.en: Modern English adds medical and computing uses such as voiding the bladder.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了医学与计算机用法，如排空膀胱。

note.en: Void shares its Latin root with vacuum and vacuous, and sits in meaning among the words that describe emptiness and lack.
note.cn: void 与 vacuum、vacuous 共享拉丁词根，在语义上位于「空」与「缺」这一组词之中。

entries.definition: a space with no matter in it at all
entries.definitionCN: 完全没有物质的真空

entries.definition: showing no real thought or content
entries.definitionCN: 空洞的；缺乏内容的

entries.definition: to keep away from something
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，词源不同；义为避开、避免

entries.definition: having nothing inside
entries.definitionCN: 里面空无一物

entries.definition: not occupied by anyone
entries.definitionCN: 无人占用的；空缺的

entries.definition: a space where something is missing
entries.definitionCN: 缺口；空缺

normalIntro.en: Void is an emptied container: the shape stays, the things inside are gone.
normalIntro.cn: void 是只被清空的容器：外形还在，里面的东西没了。

normal.en: Legal partnership of the two words came first: null and void means having no effect.
normal.cn: 两个词连用作法律用语：null and void 表示无效、作废。

normal.en: Avoid and void look close: one keeps away from, the other leaves nothing inside.
normal.cn: avoid 与 void 形态相近：一个表示避开，一个表示里面什么都没有。

normal.en: The word shares a root with vacuum, the machine that leaves a space empty.
normal.cn: 该词与 vacuum 同根，后者正是把空间抽空的机器。

normal.en: Void of means lacking that quality, as in a speech void of feeling.
normal.cn: void of 表示缺乏某种品质，例如一段毫无感情的讲话。

normal.en: To void a ticket is to cancel it, so the travel document becomes worthless.
normal.cn: void 一张车票就是把它作废，让这张凭证失去价值。

abstract.en: Picture a glass jar with lid open and nothing shining inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一只开着盖的玻璃罐，里面空得反不了光。

abstract.en: Imagine a favourite chair in a dark room with the owner gone.
abstract.cn: 想象一间暗屋里那把常坐的椅子，主人已经离开。

abstract.en: See a signed contract turning grey and blank as a stamp falls on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一份签好的合同，一枚印章落下后纸面变灰变空。

examples.en: The agreement was ruled void by the court.
examples.cn: 法院裁定这份协议无效。

examples.en: Her departure left a void in the small team.
examples.cn: 她的离开给这个小团队留下了一片空缺。

examples.en: The hall was void of sound on a quiet winter morning.
examples.cn: 在一个安静的冬日早晨，大厅里静得没有一点声音。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「挖的」——把东西全部挖走，地上一片空空；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 vacuus（空的）、vacare（空着）→ 古法语 voide、vuide（空的）→ 中古英语 voide → 英语 void，核心义「被清空之后什么都没有留下」。

sensesIntro.en: Void starts from physical emptiness, widens into the felt gap of loss, then into the lack of legal force and of a quality, and finally into a verb of emptying.
sensesIntro.cn: void 从物理上的「空」出发，扩展为失去后的空缺感受，再延伸到法律效力和品质的缺失，最后发展出「掏空、排出」的动词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a container that has been emptied out.
core.cn: 核心意象：被倒空的容器。

branches.en: Plain physical emptiness is the base sense.
branches.cn: 纯粹的物理之空是基础义项。

branches.en: A felt absence grows out of the emptied space.
branches.cn: 可感受的缺席从空出来的位置中生长出来。

branches.en: Lack of legal force and lack of quality are two abstract gaps.
branches.cn: 法律效力的缺失与品质的缺失是两种抽象的空缺。

branches.en: The verb empties a contract of force or a body of waste.
branches.cn: 动词义是掏空合同的效力，或排空身体的废物。

branches.en: Both an emptied room and the dark universe share the same hollow.
branches.cn: 空屋与黑暗宇宙共享同一种空荡。

intro.en: Void is a Latin emptiness word whose family members, vacuum, vacuous, and vacate all keep the idea of something being left empty.
intro.cn: void 是拉丁语里表示「空」的词，vacuum、vacuous 与 vacate 都保留了「被空出来」的意思。

latinIntro.en: Latin vacuus means empty and vacare means to be without; English borrowed the family twice, through French and directly from Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vacuus 意为空的，vacare 意为空着；英语分两路借入这个词族，一路经法语，一路直接取自拉丁语。

items.example: Vacuus yields the French base of void.
items.exampleCN: vacuus 提供 void 的法语来源。

items.example: Vacare lies behind words about being free of work.
items.exampleCN: vacare 是表示「不用工作」的词的源头。

items.example: Vacuum keeps the purest image of emptiness.
items.exampleCN: vacuum 保留了最纯粹的「空」意象。

items.example: Void keeps the old French ending.
items.exampleCN: void 保留了古法语的读音与拼写。

items.example: The suffix -ance forms voidance.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ance 构成 voidance。

items.meaningCN: 表示已完成或被动状态的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ed forms voided.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 voided。

items.example: Vacuous borrows the same root directly.
items.exampleCN: vacuous 直接取自同一词根。

items.example: Vacate means to leave a room empty.
items.exampleCN: vacate 意为把房间腾空。

items.example: Vacation keeps the sense of being free.
items.exampleCN: vacation 保留了「空闲」的意思。

items.meaning: to empty a place of people
items.example: Evacuate adds the prefix e- to emptying.
items.exampleCN: evacuate 在「空」前加了前缀 e-。

definition_zh: 呕吐；呕出；呕吐物；喷出
definition_en: to throw up food from the stomach through the mouth
core_image: 胃里翻搅的东西猛地从嘴里冲出来
scene: 小船在风浪里上下颠簸，乘客脸色发白，捂着嘴弯下腰。The passenger leaned over the rail and vomited into the sea.
sceneCN: 这里 vomit 是「呕吐」（第 1 个义项：把胃里的东西吐出来）；句意：乘客俯身在栏杆边，对着大海呕吐。

collocations.phrase: vomit the contents of the stomach

derivatives.zh: 由 vomit 加 -ing 构成，义为「呕吐」这一动作或症状
借自拉丁语 vomitus，医学术语，义为「呕吐物」
由 vomit 加 -ive 构成，义为「催吐的」，指引起呕吐的

senses.title: To throw up from the stomach
senses.definition: to bring food or liquid up from the stomach and out through the mouth
senses.definitionCN: 把胃里的食物或液体经口排出
senses.example: He ate spoiled fish and vomited all night.
senses.exampleCN: 他吃了变质的鱼，吐了一整夜。
senses.why: The Latin verb vomere means to throw up, and the stomach pushing its contents out is the base image.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 vomere 意为「吐出」，胃把内容物向上推出就是这个词的基础意象。

senses.title: To send out in a rush
senses.definition: to pour out or be sent out suddenly and in large amounts, especially smoke or flames
senses.definitionCN: 尤指烟或火焰突然大量地涌出或喷出
senses.example: Thick black smoke vomited from the chimney.
senses.exampleCN: 浓黑的黑烟从烟囱里喷涌而出。
senses.why: Anything forced out violently looks like what a stomach expels, so smoke and lava borrow the motion.
senses.whyCN: 任何被猛烈排出的东西都像是在呕吐，于是浓烟与熔岩借用了这个动作。

senses.title: The matter thrown up
senses.definition: the food and liquid that a person or animal brings up from the stomach
senses.definitionCN: 人或动物从胃里吐出来的食物和液体
senses.example: The nurses cleaned the vomit from the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 护士们清理了地板上的呕吐物。
senses.why: The same Latin word names both the action and its result, so the verb became a noun.
senses.whyCN: 同一个拉丁词既指动作又指结果，于是动词顺理成章地变成了名词。

intro.en: Vomit comes from Latin vomitus, a throwing up, from the verb vomere, to throw up, itself from an older root meaning to spit.
intro.cn: vomit 来自拉丁语 vomitus（呕吐），出自动词 vomere（吐出），更早可追溯到意为「吐唾沫」的词根。

items.en: Reconstructed forms such as wemh- suggest the sense to vomit or to spew.
items.cn: 重构形式 wemh- 一般认为表示「呕吐、喷出」。

items.en: Vomere means to throw up, and vomitus names the act of doing so.
items.cn: vomere 意为吐出，vomitus 指呕吐这一行为。

items.en: The verb arrives in French as vomir, used for throwing up from the stomach.
items.cn: 动词在法语中作 vomir，表示吐出胃里的东西。

items.en: English borrows the word and writes it as vomyt or vomite.
items.cn: 英语借入这个词，拼作 vomyt 或 vomite。

items.en: Modern medical writing fixes both the verb and the noun vomit.
items.cn: 现代医学写作固定了动词与名词两种用法。

note.en: Vomit is the medical and neutral word for throwing up, close in form to vomitus and in meaning to the everyday phrasal verbs for being sick.
note.cn: vomit 是表示「呕吐」的医学中性词，形式上与 vomitus 相近，意思上与日常说法相邻。

entries.definition: the matter thrown up from the stomach
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，医学术语，指呕吐物

entries.definition: causing vomiting
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，义为催吐的

entries.definition: to send out light, sound, or gas
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写与发音相近，词源不同；义为发出、排放

entries.definition: to vomit
entries.definitionCN: 非正式说法，指呕吐

entries.definition: to make the movements of vomiting without bringing anything up
entries.definitionCN: 干呕，只做呕吐动作却吐不出东西

entries.definition: the feeling that you are about to vomit
entries.definitionCN: 恶心，想呕吐的感觉

normalIntro.en: Vomit keeps the oldest meaning of its root: something forced up and thrown out.
normalIntro.cn: vomit 保留了词根最古老的意思：被用力向上推出、吐出来的东西。

normal.en: The medical record writes vomiting as the formal name of the symptom.
normal.cn: 病历上用 vomiting 作为这一症状的正式名称。

normal.en: Vomit blood is a phrase nurses learn early, because it signals danger.
normal.cn: vomit blood 是护士很早就记住的说法，因为它意味着危险。

normal.en: The noun is uncountable for the matter, while a vomit is one episode.
normal.cn: 指呕吐物时名词不可数，而 a vomit 指一次呕吐。

normal.en: Nausea names the feeling, vomit names the act that may follow.
normal.cn: nausea 指恶心的感觉，vomit 指随后可能发生的动作。

normal.en: Spelling note: the final syllable takes a single it, as in limit, not two.
normal.cn: 拼写提示：末尾音节只有一个 it，与 limit 类似，不要写成两个 t 的组合。

abstract.en: Picture a wave rolling upward inside the body and breaking at the mouth.
abstract.cn: 想象身体里一道浪向上翻涌，最后在嘴边破开。

abstract.en: Imagine a volcano pushing dark ash into the sky through a narrow throat.
abstract.cn: 想象一座火山从狭窄的喉口把黑灰推向天空。

abstract.en: See a wet stain on the floor that someone must clean with a bucket.
abstract.cn: 想象地上一摊湿渍，必须有人提着水桶来清理。

examples.en: The medicine made him vomit within minutes.
examples.cn: 药让他几分钟内就吐了。

examples.en: Lava vomited from the crater during the eruption.
examples.cn: 爆发期间熔岩从火山口喷涌而出。

examples.en: She was told to stay in bed after a night of vomiting.
examples.cn: 吐了一整夜之后，她被要求卧床休息。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我密吐」——我偷偷密密地吐了出来；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 印欧词根 wemh-（一般认为意为「吐」）→ 拉丁语 vomere（吐出）→ vomitus（呕吐）→ 古法语 vomir → 英语 vomit，核心义「胃里翻搅的东西向上冲出来」。

sensesIntro.en: Vomit begins with the body throwing up, widens to anything erupting outward, and finally names the matter brought up.
sensesIntro.cn: vomit 先指身体把胃里的东西吐出来，再扩展到任何向外喷涌的东西，最后指吐出的物质本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: food forced upward and out through the mouth.
core.cn: 核心意象：食物被向上顶出，从嘴里喷出。

branches.en: The body throwing up is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 身体呕吐是字面义项。

branches.en: Anything bursting outward borrows the same motion.
branches.cn: 任何向外爆出的东西都借用了同一个动作。

branches.en: The substance that comes up becomes a noun.
branches.cn: 被吐出来的东西变成了名词。

branches.en: The act and its result are named by the same Latin word.
branches.cn: 动作和结果由同一个拉丁词命名。

branches.en: Smoke pouring out and food thrown up both leave a mass behind.
branches.cn: 喷射的浓烟与吐出的食物都会留下一团物质。

intro.en: Vomit is a Latin throwing up word, with English offspring such as vomiting, vomitus, and the adjective vomitive.
intro.cn: vomit 是拉丁语中表示「吐出」的词，英语中衍生出 vomiting、vomitus 与形容词 vomitive。

latinIntro.en: Latin vomere means to throw up, and its noun vomitus shares the stem with the English adjective vomitive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vomere 意为吐出，其名词 vomitus 与英语形容词 vomitive 共用同一个词干。

items.example: Vomere is the direct verb source.
items.exampleCN: vomere 是直接的动词来源。

items.example: Vomitus gives the English medical noun.
items.exampleCN: vomitus 提供了英语的医学名词。

items.example: Vomit regularises the old Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: vomit 把这古老的拉丁动词规则化了。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或过程的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms vomiting.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 vomiting。

items.example: The suffix -ive forms vomitive.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ive 构成 vomitive。

items.example: Emetic is a near synonym from Greek.
items.exampleCN: emetic 是来自希腊语的近义词。

items.example: Nausea names the feeling before vomiting.
items.exampleCN: nausea 指呕吐之前的恶心感。

items.example: Vomica is an old medical relative from the same root.
items.exampleCN: vomica 是同源的古老医学术语。

items.example: Retching is the act without any result.
items.exampleCN: retching 是只有动作没有结果的干呕。

definition_zh: 航行；航海；旅行；（宇航）飞行
definition_en: a long journey by sea or through space
core_image: 一艘帆船驶离港口，向远方的海平线驶去
scene: 港口上风很大，水手们松开缆绳，帆鼓满了风，船慢慢离开码头。The sailors set out on a long voyage across the Pacific.
sceneCN: 这里 voyage 是「航行」（第 1 个义项：经海路的长途旅程）；句意：水手们出发，开始一次横渡太平洋的漫长航行。

pos.zh: 航行；航海；旅行；宇航飞行

derivatives.zh: 由 voyage 加施事后缀 -er 构成，义为「航海者；宇航员」
由法语 bon（好）加 voyage 构成的外来祝福语，意为「一路顺风」
借自法语 voyageur（旅行者），特指北美早期乘独木舟运送毛皮的商人

senses.title: A long journey by sea
senses.definition: a long journey, especially one made by ship across water
senses.definitionCN: 尤指乘船渡水的长途旅程
senses.example: The voyage from Lisbon to India took many months.
senses.exampleCN: 从里斯本到印度的航行花了很长时间。
senses.why: The Old French verb voier means to travel by way, and a journey across water naturally keeps the name.
senses.whyCN: 古法语动词 voier 意为「沿路旅行」，渡水的旅程自然沿用了这个名称。

senses.title: A journey through space
senses.definition: a journey made by a spacecraft through space, or by a probe to another planet
senses.definitionCN: 航天器穿越太空的飞行，或探测器飞往另一颗行星
senses.example: The probe began its voyage to Mars last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 探测器去年春天开始了飞往火星的航程。
senses.why: Water gave way to space, but the long open journey between two points kept the same image.
senses.whyCN: 水换成了太空，但两点之间那段漫长空阔的旅程保留了同一个意象。

senses.title: A mental journey
senses.definition: a long experience or process in life, written about like a sea crossing
senses.definitionCN: 人生中漫长的经历或过程，被比作一次渡海
senses.example: Her voyage through grief lasted several years.
senses.exampleCN: 她走出悲伤的历程持续了好几年。
senses.why: Once a voyage is a long crossing, any hard passage of life can be imagined as one.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 voyage 成为漫长渡海，人生中任何艰难的历程都可以被想象成一次航行。

intro.en: Voyage comes from Old French voiage, a journey, from Latin viaticum, provisions for a road, from via, a road.
intro.cn: voyage 来自古法语 voiage（旅程），出自拉丁语 viaticum（路上的给养），而 viaticum 源于 via（道路）。

items.en: Via means a road, and viaticum means what is needed for the way.
items.cn: via 意为道路，viaticum 意为路上所需的给养。

items.en: Voiage names any journey, whether on land or by sea.
items.cn: voiage 泛指任何旅程，无论陆路还是海路。

items.en: The word enters English first as voiage, a journey.
items.cn: 该词在十三世纪进入英语，写作 voiage，即旅程。

items.en: Writers narrow it to long journeys by water.
items.cn: 作家们逐渐把它缩小到长途水上旅行。

items.en: Modern English extends the word to journeys through space.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到穿越太空的飞行。

note.en: Voyage keeps the Latin road via at its heart and sits between travel words and ocean crossing words.
note.cn: voyage 的核心是拉丁语道路 via，在语义上处于旅行词与渡海词之间。

entries.definition: a person who makes a long journey
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，指远航者、宇航员

entries.definition: provisions for a journey
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，拉丁语，指旅途的给养

entries.definition: the flying of aircraft
entries.definitionCN: 只是发音相近，词源不同；义为航空

entries.definition: the act of travelling from one place to another
entries.definitionCN: 从一地到另一地的旅行

entries.definition: a pleasure trip by ship visiting several ports
entries.definitionCN: 游览若干港口的乘船旅行

entries.definition: a short trip across a stretch of water
entries.definitionCN: 横渡一段水域的短程旅行

normalIntro.en: Voyage grew from the Latin word for a road, so every voyage is a road laid on water or on the dark of space.
normalIntro.cn: voyage 源自拉丁语里表示「道路」的词，所以每一次航行都是在水面或黑暗太空中铺出的一条路。

normal.en: Maiden voyage names a ship first sea trip, often the one people worry about.
normal.cn: maiden voyage 指一艘船的首次出海，也常是人们最担心的一次。

normal.en: The phrase bon voyage literally wishes a good journey.
normal.cn: 法语告别语 bon voyage 字面意思就是祝旅程顺利。

normal.en: A voyager is anyone who crosses long distances, including a spacecraft passenger.
normal.cn: voyager 指跨越遥远的旅人，也包括航天器上的乘员。

normal.en: Compare via and voyage: both keep the picture of a road.
normal.cn: 比较 via 与 voyage：两者都保留着「道路」的画面。

normal.en: For a ship the count is one voyage out and another voyage back.
normal.cn: 对船来说，去程算一次 voyage，回程再算一次。

abstract.en: Picture a paper chart with a dotted line from one harbour to another.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸质海图，虚线从一个港口画到另一个港口。

abstract.en: See a silver probe turning slowly and then firing away from the Earth.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚银色探测器缓缓转身，随后从地球身旁飞走。

abstract.en: Imagine a line of small footprints leading through fog toward grey light.
abstract.cn: 想象一串小脚印穿过浓雾，走向灰色的天光。

examples.en: The ship made its maiden voyage in the spring.
examples.cn: 这艘船在春天进行了首航。

examples.en: Columbus recorded the events of the voyage in a logbook.
examples.cn: 哥伦布把这次航行中的事件记录在航海日志里。

examples.en: The crew voyaged for nearly a year before reaching land.
examples.cn: 船员们航行了将近一年才抵达陆地。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我爷」——我爷年轻时坐船远航；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 via（道路）→ viaticum（上路前的给养）→ 古法语 voiage（旅程）→ 中古英语 voiage（旅程）→ 航海义固定，核心义「沿路远行，尤指渡海」。

sensesIntro.en: Voyage starts as a long sea journey, moves to journeys in space, and then serves as a picture for long processes in a life.
sensesIntro.cn: voyage 先指漫长的海上旅程，再指太空中的航程，最后被用来比喻人生中漫长的历程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ship sailing away from a harbour toward open water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一艘船驶离港口，投向开阔的海面。

branches.en: The long sea crossing is the central sense.
branches.cn: 漫长的渡海是核心义项。

branches.en: Space travel borrows the crossing image.
branches.cn: 太空飞行借用了这种穿越的意象。

branches.en: A hard passage in life is described as a voyage.
branches.cn: 人生中艰难的历程也被说成一次航行。

branches.en: A ship and a probe both leave one point for a distant one.
branches.cn: 船与探测器都从一点出发前往遥远的一点。

branches.en: Going somewhere and changing along the way share the same frame.
branches.cn: 去往某地与沿途改变共享同一个框架。

intro.en: Voyage is a Latin road word, and English builds around it with voyager and the borrowed French phrase bon voyage.
intro.cn: voyage 是拉丁语中表示「道路」的词，英语围绕它构成 voyager，并借入法语短语 bon voyage。

latinIntro.en: Latin via means road, and viaticum means the supplies taken for a journey.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 via 意为道路，viaticum 意为为旅程准备的给养。

items.example: Via is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: via 是整个词族的根。

items.example: Viaticum literally means for the road.
items.exampleCN: viaticum 字面意思就是「路上用的」。

items.example: Voiage is the French form that reached English.
items.exampleCN: voiage 是进入英语的法语形式。

items.example: Voyage narrows the journey to the sea.
items.exampleCN: voyage 把旅程缩小到海上。

items.meaningCN: 表示「做某事的人」的词尾
items.example: The suffix -er forms voyager.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 voyager。

items.meaning: a traveller on a long journey
items.example: Voyager also names two famous spacecraft.
items.exampleCN: voyager 也是两艘著名航天器的名字。

items.example: Bon belongs to the borrowed phrase of farewell.
items.exampleCN: bon 属于借入的告别短语。

items.meaning: to turn away from a way
items.example: Deviate keeps via under the prefix de-.
items.exampleCN: deviate 在前缀 de- 之后保留了 via。

items.meaning: to clear a difficulty out of the way
items.example: Obviate means to meet a thing on the way.
items.exampleCN: obviate 原意是在路上迎面遇上。

items.example: Convey comes by way of the same via.
items.exampleCN: convey 同样经由 via 演变而来。

items.example: Trivial once meant at the crossroads, from tri plus via.
items.exampleCN: trivial 原意是「三岔路口的」，由 tri 加 via 构成。

definition_zh: 庸俗的；粗俗的；下流的；平民的；通俗的
definition_en: lacking good taste or polite manners, or belonging to the ordinary common people
core_image: 街市上人群中一声粗野的吆喝，把精致的谈吐压得没了声
scene: 宴席上有人高声讲了个粗俗的笑话，满桌人顿时安静下来。The host was embarrassed by the vulgar joke told over dinner.
sceneCN: 这里 vulgar 是「粗俗的、下流的」（第 1 个义项：言谈举止缺乏品味、冒犯他人）；句意：主人在晚餐时讲的那个粗俗笑话让他很尴尬。图中可辨识物件：酒杯、餐桌、尴尬的人群。

collocations.zh: 通俗语言；本国语言；常用于宗教或学术语境

derivatives.zh: 由 vulgar 加后缀 -ity 构成，义为「粗俗；庸俗；粗俗的话」
由 vulgar 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「粗俗地」
由 vulgar 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「使通俗化；使低俗化」
由 vulgar 加 -ism 构成，义为「粗俗词语；粗俗用语」
vulgarize 的英式名词形式，义为「通俗化」

senses.title: Offensively rude or crude
senses.definition: rude, crude, or indecent in a way that offends polite people
senses.definitionCN: 言谈举止粗野、不雅，会冒犯讲究礼貌的人
senses.example: Please avoid using vulgar language in the classroom.
senses.exampleCN: 请不要在教室里使用粗俗的语言。
senses.why: The Latin source means belonging to the crowd, and what the crowd does in public was long thought to lack refinement.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源指「属于人群的」，而人群在公共场所的言行长久以来被认为缺少教养，冒犯感由此而来。

senses.title: Lacking good taste
senses.definition: showing poor taste, especially by being showy or insensitive
senses.definitionCN: 品味低劣，尤指炫耀、招摇或欠缺分寸
senses.example: The gold statues in the garden look rather vulgar.
senses.exampleCN: 花园里的镀金雕像显得有些俗气。
senses.why: Common taste was once treated as the opposite of courtly taste, so the same crowd label came to mean tasteless.
senses.whyCN: 大众品味曾被视为宫廷品味的反面，于是同一个「人群的」标签也引申出「没品味」。

senses.title: Relating to ordinary people
senses.definition: connected with the common people rather than the wealthy or educated classes
senses.definitionCN: 与普通百姓相关，而非富贵或有教养的阶层
senses.example: The term vulgar Latin names the everyday speech of the Roman provinces.
senses.exampleCN: 「通俗拉丁语」这一术语指的是罗马各行省的日常口语。
senses.why: This is the original Latin sense, still kept in historical and legal phrases about the common people.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁语本义，至今仍保留在涉及平民的历史与法律短语中。

senses.title: Spoken in the common language
senses.definition: expressed in the everyday tongue of the people rather than in Latin or another learned language
senses.definitionCN: 用百姓的日常语言表达，而不是拉丁语等学术语言
senses.example: Early church writers put the Bible into the vulgar tongue so that all could read it.
senses.exampleCN: 早期教会的作者把圣经译成本地俗语，让人人都能读懂。
senses.why: When learned texts stayed in Latin, writing in the language of the crowd was a radical choice, and the word marks it.
senses.whyCN: 学术文本长期使用拉丁语，用大众语言写作曾是很激进的选择，这个词正好标记了这种选择。

intro.en: Vulgar comes from Latin vulgar, a short form of vulgare, from vulgus, the common people; the path into English is through dated French and Latin again.
intro.cn: vulgar 来自拉丁语 vulgare 的短形式，而 vulgare 又出自 vulgus（平民、大众）；它经由早期法语进入英语，之后又受到拉丁语原形的影响。

items.en: Vulgus means the ordinary crowd or the common people.
items.cn: vulgus 指普通民众、平民大众。

items.en: Vulgaris, an adjective from vulgus, means common or ordinary.
items.cn: 由 vulgus 派生的形容词 vulgaris 意为「普通的、大众的」。

items.en: The French word arrives in English with the sense common or ordinary.
items.cn: 这个词以「普通的、一般的」之意从古法语进入英语。

items.en: The Latin form restores the old vowel pattern, and the sense shifts to the language of the people.
items.cn: 拉丁词形使旧有的元音拼法重新出现，词义转向「百姓的语言」。

items.en: From the crowd at large grows the modern core: coarse, tasteless, or indecent.
items.cn: 从「大众群体」这一本义发展出现代核心义：粗俗、没品味、不雅。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same Latin crowd root; the near-meaning group gathers other words for poor taste and bad manners.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁语「人群」词根构成的词族；近义组收其它表示品味低、举止粗的词，彼此轻重不同。

entries.definition: The quality of being vulgar, or an instance of vulgar behaviour or speech.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「粗俗、庸俗」，也可指一句粗话或一个粗俗举动，由本词加后缀构成。

entries.definition: To make something popular in a simple form, or to make it coarse.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使通俗化」，也可指「使低俗化」，由本词加后缀构词。

entries.definition: A Latin Bible version known as the Vulgate; it looks like this word but is a separate church name.
entries.definitionCN: 专名词，指通行的拉丁文圣经译本；拼写相近，但属教会专名，词义与本词无关。

entries.definition: To reveal a secret; it looks related but comes from a different Latin root.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「泄露秘密」；拼写有相似成分，但词源不同，只是形近。

entries.definition: Offensive because it deals with sex in a shocking way; stronger than vulgar.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「淫秽的、猥亵的」，指内容涉及性而令人反感，比 vulgar 更重。

entries.definition: Rough in texture or in manners; keeps a physical image of roughness.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「粗糙的、粗鲁的」，既指质地也指言行，保留「粗糙」的具象感。

entries.definition: Unrefined or lacking polish, from raw materials to blunt words.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「粗糙的、粗野的」，从原材料到生硬的言辞都可用。

entries.definition: Lacking good taste or delicate judgment; focuses on style rather than manners.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「没品味的」，侧重审美格调，而非举止礼貌。

normalIntro.en: These hooks rely on the real Latin root for the crowd and on the phrases the word actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子基于真实的拉丁语「人群」词根，以及这个词实际保留的搭配。

normal.en: Vulgus is the crowd, so vulgar is literally what the crowd does in the street.
normal.cn: vulgus 就是人群，所以 vulgar 字面就是「人群在街头会做的事」。

normal.en: Vulgar language, vulgar jokes, and vulgar taste form a single family of bad manners.
normal.cn: 粗话、下流笑话、庸俗品味，构成同一类「不得体」。

normal.en: Keep the pair vulgar and elegant in mind: each word needs the other to mean anything.
normal.cn: 把 vulgar 与 elegant 配对记：一个说没品味，一个说有品味。

normal.en: The phrase the vulgar tongue still means the language of ordinary people, not a rude phrase.
normal.cn: 短语 the vulgar tongue 至今指「平民的日常语言」，不是粗话。

normal.en: Compare vulgar with obscene and coarse: vulgar is bad manners, obscene is sexual shock, coarse is roughness.
normal.cn: 对比 obscene 与 coarse：vulgar 缺教养，obscene 涉淫秽，coarse 强调粗糙。

abstract.en: Picture a crowded market where one voice shouts a rude joke over the polite chatter.
abstract.cn: 想象一个拥挤的集市，一个声音在礼貌的寒暄之上喊出一句粗笑话。

abstract.en: Imagine a gallery of fine paintings with one gaudy poster pasted in the middle.
abstract.cn: 想象一间挂满精品画的展厅，正中贴着一张艳俗的海报。

abstract.en: Think of a scholar reading a Latin text aloud, then switching to the local dialect for everyone to follow.
abstract.cn: 想象一位学者先朗读拉丁文，再换成方言，让所有人都听得懂。

examples.en: The film was criticised for its vulgar jokes about illness.
examples.cn: 这部电影因拿疾病开玩笑的粗俗桥段而受到批评。

examples.en: He was a vulgar man who measured success only by the size of his car.
examples.cn: 他是个庸俗的人，衡量成功只看车子的大小。

examples.en: Medieval scholars often wrote in the vulgar tongue so that ordinary readers could follow.
examples.cn: 中世纪的学者常写成本地俗语，让普通读者也能读懂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「挖高」——把嗓门挖得老高，当街粗声粗气地喊：粗俗的、没教养的

root: 拉丁语 vulgus「平民、大众」→ 形容词 vulgaris「普通的、大众的」→ 古法语 → 英语 vulgar；核心义是「属于人群的」，由此分化出「大众的、通俗的」与「缺乏教养的、粗俗的」两支。

sensesIntro.en: Vulgar first means rude and indecent, then tasteless, and in older or technical uses it still means of the common people and written in their everyday language.
sensesIntro.cn: vulgar 首先指粗鲁不雅，其次指品味低俗；在较早或专门的用法中，它仍指「平民的」和「用百姓日常语言写的」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rough shout from a crowded market rises over the polite chatter of a refined room.
core.cn: 核心意象：嘈杂集市上的一声粗吼盖过了体面人的轻声细语。

branches.en: Rudeness is the modern everyday sense built on the crowd label.
branches.cn: 粗鲁不雅是由「人群」标签长出的现代日常义。

branches.en: Tasteless display comes from treating common taste as the low end of style.
branches.cn: 俗气招摇来自把大众品味当作格调的下端。

branches.en: The historical sense keeps the Latin meaning of ordinary people.
branches.cn: 历史义保留了拉丁语「普通人」的本义。

branches.en: Writing in the vulgar tongue is the plain-speech sense now heard in church history.
branches.cn: 用俗语写作就是通俗语言这一支，如今多见于教会史。

branches.en: A vulgar joke and a vulgar statue both break the same unwritten rule of restraint.
branches.cn: 下流笑话和俗气雕像都违反了同一条「克制」的隐形规矩。

intro.en: Vulgar is built on the Latin noun for the crowd, with English words for the quality, the manner, the act and the simplified version around it.
intro.cn: vulgar 建立在拉丁语「人群」名词之上，英语围绕它构成表性质、方式、动作与简化版的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vulgus means the common people, and vulgaris means common or ordinary.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vulgus 意为「平民、大众」，vulgaris 意为「普通的、大众的」。

items.example: Vulgus supplies the crowd image.
items.exampleCN: vulgus 提供「人群」的意象。

items.example: Vulgaris is the adjective built from vulgus.
items.exampleCN: vulgaris 是由 vulgus 构成的形容词。

items.meaning: to make common, to spread among people
items.meaningCN: 使大众化；在民众中传播
items.example: Vulgare underlies the modern verbs of spreading.
items.exampleCN: vulgare 是表「传播」的现代动词的基础。

items.meaning: rude, tasteless, of the common people
items.example: Vulgar carries the plain adjective sense.
items.exampleCN: vulgar 承载核心形容词义。

items.meaningCN: 表示性质或状态的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ity forms vulgarity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 vulgarity。

items.example: Vulgarity names the whole quality.
items.exampleCN: vulgarity 指粗俗这一整体性质。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms vulgarly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 vulgarly。

items.meaning: to make, to cause to be
items.example: The suffix -ize forms vulgarize and vulgarise.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ize 构成 vulgarize 与 vulgarise。

items.example: Vulgarize turns the adjective into an action.
items.exampleCN: vulgarize 把形容词变成动作。

items.meaning: a practice or a particular usage
items.meaningCN: 表示做法或某种用法的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ism forms vulgarism.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ism 构成 vulgarism。

definition_zh: 秃鹫；坐收渔利者；趁人之危的人
definition_en: a large bird that feeds on dead animals, or a person who takes advantage of others in trouble
core_image: 一具倒下的兽尸上空，黑色的大鸟慢慢盘绕，等着落下
scene: 沙漠公路旁躺着一头死去的骆驼，几只大鸟在天上盘旋。A pair of vultures circled lower and lower over the dead camel.
sceneCN: 这里 vulture 是「秃鹫」（第 1 个义项：以动物尸体为食的大型猛禽）；句意：一对秃鹫绕着死去的骆驼越飞越低。图中可辨识物件：沙漠公路、骆驼尸体、盘旋的鸟影。

pos.zh: 坐收渔利者；趁人之危的人

collocations.zh: 文化掠夺者；附庸风雅的人，略带戏谑
秃鹫基金；专门低价收购困境债务的投资基金

derivatives.zh: 由 vulture 加形容词后缀 -ine 构成，义为「秃鹫般的；贪婪的」
由 vulture 加后缀 -ous 构成，义为「鹰鹫般的；掠夺的」
由 vulture 加 -ism 构成，义为「掠夺行径；趁火打劫的做派」

senses.title: A large bird that eats carrion
senses.definition: a large bird of prey that feeds mainly on the flesh of dead animals
senses.definitionCN: 以动物尸体为主食的大型猛禽
senses.example: A vulture landed beside the carcass and tore at the skin.
senses.exampleCN: 一只秃鹫落在兽尸旁，撕扯着皮肉。
senses.why: The Latin name for the bird is close to the word for a tear, so the image of ripping flesh is built into the name.
senses.whyCN: 这个鸟的拉丁名与「撕裂」一词相近，所以「扯开血肉」的画面从一开始就藏在名字里。

senses.title: A person who gains from others misfortune
senses.titleCN: 坐收渔利者；趁人之危的人
senses.definition: a person who waits for others to suffer and then profits from the damage
senses.definitionCN: 等别人遭难、再从损失中获利的人
senses.example: Politicians were described as vultures feeding on the city crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 有人把那些政客形容成靠城市危机饱食的秃鹫。
senses.why: The bird waits for the fall and then takes its share, which is exactly how the metaphor describes exploiters.
senses.whyCN: 这种鸟会等在猎物倒下之后再分食，这一行为正好映射了「坐等别人倒霉再取利」的剥削者。

senses.title: A buyer who prey on debtors
senses.definition: an investor or fund that buys distressed debt or assets cheaply and demands full payment
senses.definitionCN: 低价购入困境债务或资产、再索要全额偿付的投资者或基金
senses.example: A vulture fund bought the poor nation debt at a fraction of its value.
senses.exampleCN: 一家秃鹫基金以极低的价格买下了这个穷国的债务。
senses.why: The same predatory patience shapes a market niche, where the fall of another business becomes the buyer gain.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「等猎物倒下」逻辑塑造出一个市场角色：别人的企业一倒，买家的收益就来了。

senses.title: A severe critic looking for flaws
senses.titleCN: 严苛的批评者；挑刺的人
senses.definition: a reviewer or critic who seems to circle a work, waiting to tear it apart
senses.definitionCN: 像绕着作品盘旋、只等着撕开它的评论者或批评家
senses.example: The director called the press vultures who lived on bad reviews.
senses.exampleCN: 这位导演称那些媒体是靠负面评论过活的秃鹫。
senses.why: The circling image extends to critics: they hover over a new work and strike when it shows weakness.
senses.whyCN: 「盘旋」这一意象延伸到批评者身上：他们绕着新作品打转，一见弱点就下手。

intro.en: Vulture comes from Latin vultur, a name for the bird, through thirteenth-century French voutre, with the Latin ending later restored.
intro.cn: vulture 来自拉丁语 vultur，是该鸟的拉丁名；经由十三世纪法语的 voutre 进入英语，后来拉丁词尾又被恢复。

items.en: Vultur names the bird of prey that feeds on carrion.
items.cn: vultur 指以腐尸为食的猛禽。

items.en: The name is associated with vellere, to tear or pull, as the bird rips flesh.
items.cn: 这个名字一般认为与 vellere（撕裂、拉扯）相关，与鸟撕扯血肉的动作呼应。

items.en: The word appears in Latin translations of the Bible, which spread its use into many languages.
items.cn: 这个词出现在圣经的拉丁文译本中，借助译本流传到多种语言。

items.en: Voutre carries the bird name into early English.
items.cn: voutre 把这个鸟名带入早期英语。

items.en: The form settles into English, written with the modern spelling later.
items.cn: 拼写逐渐在英语中定型，现代形式在后世确定下来。

items.en: From the bird grows the metaphor for people who profit from another decline.
items.cn: 从鸟义发展出比喻义，指靠别人倒下而获利的人。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the Latin bird name and near-spellings; the near-meaning group gathers scavengers and profiteers.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁鸟名词族与拼写相近的词；近义组收同为食腐的鸟以及不同强度的剥削者说法。

entries.definition: Adjective meaning like a vulture, especially in being greedy or predatory.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「秃鹫般的、贪婪掠夺的」，由本词加后缀构成。

entries.definition: Rude or tasteless; it begins with the same letters but comes from the crowd root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「粗俗的、庸俗的」；只是开头字母相同，词源来自「人群」词根，与本词无关。

entries.definition: To make something popular in a simple form; another crowd word with a similar opening.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使通俗化」；同样以 vul- 开头，但属于「人群」词族，只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: The customs and arts of a society; it rhymes with this word but has no connection.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「文化、习俗」；与 vulture 押韵，只是拼写与读音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Any animal or person that feeds on dead matter or waste.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「食腐动物；拾荒者」，范围比 vulture 更宽。

entries.definition: A huge New World bird that also feeds on carrion and glides high.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「神鹰」，同为新大陆的大型食腐鸟，常高飞滑翔。

entries.definition: A large bird of prey that hunts live animals rather than eating carrion.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「鹰」，同为大型猛禽，但捕食活物，而非食腐。

entries.definition: A person who makes unfair profit from a crisis; a plain word for the money sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「投机商、发国难财者」，是对「坐收渔利」这一义项的白描说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin bird name and the phrases the word keeps today.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子基于真实的拉丁鸟名，以及这个词如今保留的搭配。

normal.en: Vultur is the Latin name of the bird, and the modern spelling keeps the sharp c sound.
normal.cn: vultur 就是这种鸟的拉丁名，现代拼写保留了词中的清辅音。

normal.en: The name links to vellere, to tear, which is what the bird does to a carcass.
normal.cn: 这个名字与 vellere「撕裂」相关，正是这种鸟对兽尸做的事。

normal.en: A vulture fund and a vulture capitalist both use the image of the bird waiting for a fall.
normal.cn: vulture fund 和 vulture capitalist 都借用了鸟「等别人倒下」的形象。

normal.en: Remember the flock phrase: vultures arrive in a crowd, not one by one.
normal.cn: 记住群体搭配：秃鹫总是一群群来，不会单独出现。

normal.en: Compare condor, eagle and owl: condor is a giant scavenger, eagle hunts, owl works at night.
normal.cn: 对比 condor、eagle 与 owl：神鹰是巨型的食腐者，鹰捕猎，猫头鹰夜里活动。

abstract.en: Picture a carcass on a desert road and a slow ring of dark wings above it.
abstract.cn: 想象沙漠公路上的一具兽尸，上方是一圈缓缓盘旋的黑翼。

abstract.en: Think of a stock chart falling while one buyer quietly waits at the bottom.
abstract.cn: 想象股票曲线一路下跌，而一个买家静静等在谷底。

abstract.en: Imagine a circle of critics around a new play, lifting their pens as the curtain rises.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈批评家围在新剧周围，幕布一升就举起笔。

examples.en: Vultures feed on carcasses that other animals leave behind.
examples.cn: 秃鹫以其它动物留下的尸体为食。

examples.en: After the factory closed, vultures swooped in to buy the machines cheaply.
examples.cn: 工厂倒闭后，一批投机者一拥而上，低价买走了机器。

examples.en: The soldiers compared the journalists to vultures waiting for a disaster.
examples.cn: 士兵们把那些记者比作等着灾难降临的秃鹫。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哇偶特」——哇偶，天上那群大鸟又特地盘旋起来：秃鹫

root: 拉丁语 vultur「秃鹫」→ 古法语 voutre → 英语 vulture；拉丁名一般认为与 vellere「撕裂、拉扯」有关，但更早的词源来源不确定。核心义「食腐的猛禽」，再引申为「靠他人遭难获利的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Vulture starts as a real bird that lives on dead flesh, then spreads to people who wait for others to fall: exploiters, distressed-debt buyers, and harsh critics.
sensesIntro.cn: vulture 首先指以死尸为食的真实鸟类，再扩展指等着别人倒下的人：剥削者、困境债务收购者与严苛的批评者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: dark wings circle above a fallen animal, waiting for their turn to feed.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑翼在倒下的动物上方盘旋，等待轮到自己进食。

branches.en: The literal bird is the starting sense of the word.
branches.cn: 真实的鸟类是这个词的起点义。

branches.en: The person who profits from a fall is the central metaphor.
branches.cn: 靠他人倒下获利的人是最核心的比喻义。

branches.en: The fund sense narrows the metaphor to distressed debt and assets.
branches.cn: 基金义把这一个比喻缩小到困境债务与资产。

branches.en: The critic sense keeps the circling image but moves it from money to reputation.
branches.cn: 批评者义保留「盘旋」意象，只是从钱转到了名声。

branches.en: All three extended senses share one pattern: someone waits for weakness and then takes.
branches.cn: 三个引申义共享同一模式：先等对方虚弱，再动手攫取。

intro.en: Vulture is a whole Latin bird name rather than a compound, and English builds a small family of adjectives and nouns on it.
intro.cn: vulture 整体是一个拉丁鸟名，不是前缀加词根的复合词；英语围绕它构成一族形容词与名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vultur means vulture, and the related verb vellere means to tear or pluck.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vultur 意为「秃鹫」，相关的动词 vellere 意为「撕裂、拔扯」。

items.example: Vultur is the direct source of the English bird name.
items.exampleCN: vultur 是英语鸟名的直接来源。

items.example: Vellere is associated with the tearing image of the bird.
items.exampleCN: vellere 与这种鸟「撕裂」的画面相联系。

items.example: Voutre is the French form that reached English.
items.exampleCN: voutre 是传入英语的法语形式。

items.example: Vulture keeps the literal bird sense.
items.exampleCN: vulture 保留字面上的鸟义。

items.example: The suffix -ine forms vulturine.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ine 构成 vulturine。

items.example: Vulturine describes a birdlike greed.
items.exampleCN: vulturine 描述鹰鹫般的贪婪。

items.example: The suffix -ous forms vulturous.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 构成 vulturous。

items.meaningCN: 表示做法或体系的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ism forms vulturism.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ism 构成 vulturism。

items.example: Vulturous is the rarer adjective form.
items.exampleCN: vulturous 是较少见的形容词形式。

definition_zh: 马甲；西装背心；西服内穿的无袖上衣
definition_en: a sleeveless garment worn over a shirt and under a jacket, formerly called a vest in British use
core_image: 一件合身的短背心套在白衬衫外，纽扣整齐地扣到胸口
scene: 婚宴上，伴郎把领带拉正，又把马甲最上一颗纽扣扣好。He fastened the top button of his waistcoat before stepping up to the stage.
sceneCN: 这里 waistcoat 是「马甲、西装背心」（第 1 个义项：穿在衬衫外、外套里的无袖上衣）；句意：他上前台之前扣好了马甲的最上一颗纽扣。图中可辨识物件：白衬衫、马甲、领带、舞台。

derivatives.zh: 由 waistcoat 加后缀 -ed 构成，义为「穿马甲的」
由 waistcoat 加 -ing 构成，义为「马甲面料」
复合词的前一半，义为「腰」，指裁剪到腰部的短上衣
复合词的后一半，义为「外套、上衣」，构成马甲这一类别的总称

senses.title: A sleeveless garment worn under a jacket
senses.definition: a close-fitting sleeveless garment for the upper body, worn over a shirt and usually under a jacket
senses.definitionCN: 贴身上身无袖衣服，穿在衬衫之外，通常还套在外套里面
senses.example: His grey waistcoat matched the lining of his jacket.
senses.exampleCN: 他的灰色马甲与外套内衬相配。
senses.why: The garment is a coat cut short at the waist, so the waist sets the whole shape.
senses.whyCN: 这种衣服是「在腰部截断的外套」，所以「腰」决定了它的整体形状。

senses.title: A part of traditional formal dress
senses.definition: the matching inner layer of traditional formal dress, often in white for very formal events
senses.definitionCN: 传统正式服装中与外套配套的内层，极正式的场合常用白色
senses.example: White waistcoats and gloves are still worn at some weddings.
senses.exampleCN: 一些婚礼上至今仍穿白色马甲并戴白手套。
senses.why: Formal dress became a fixed set of layers, and the middle layer got its own rules of colour and cut.
senses.whyCN: 正式服装逐渐固定为分层穿着，中间这一层马甲便有了自己的颜色与剪裁规矩。

senses.title: A close fitting garment called a vest in America
senses.definition: the same inner garment when described north of the Atlantic, where it is usually called a vest
senses.definitionCN: 同一件内穿的无袖上衣，在北美通常称为 vest
senses.example: British shops sell waistcoats, while American shops sell vests.
senses.exampleCN: 英国商店卖 waistcoat，美国商店同样款式叫 vest。
senses.why: The same article of clothing kept two different names on two shores, and only one of them keeps the waist image.
senses.whyCN: 同一件衣服在大西洋两岸保留了两种叫法，只有英国说法保留「腰」这一形象。

senses.title: A knitted woollen waistcoat
senses.definition: a knitted or woollen sleeveless top worn for warmth, especially in British country wear
senses.definitionCN: 保暖用的针织或羊毛无袖上衣，尤见于英国乡村穿着
senses.example: The shepherd pulled on a thick waistcoat before going out into the snow.
senses.exampleCN: 牧羊人出门走进雪地前套上了一件厚厚的羊毛背心。
senses.why: The waist cut that began with tailoring moved to knitwear, where the same short layer keeps the chest warm.
senses.whyCN: 从裁缝开始的「截到腰部」这种做法移到了毛衣上，同样的一层短衣护住了胸口。

intro.en: Waistcoat is an English compound of waist and coat, a coat cut to the waist, first recorded in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: waistcoat 是英语自造的复合词，由 waist（腰）与 coat（外套）合成，义为「截到腰部的上衣」，首见于十七世纪。

items.en: Waist appears as an English word for the part of the body above the hips.
items.cn: waist 在古英语中已出现，指腰以上的身体部位。

items.en: Coate reaches English from French, meaning a long outer garment.
items.cn: coate 从法语进入英语，指一种长外衣。

items.en: Tailors begin cutting coats short at the waist, and the shape is named for it.
items.cn: 裁缝开始把外套裁短到腰部，样式因此得名。

items.en: Waistcoat is recorded as the name of the short sleeveless garment worn under the coat.
items.cn: waistcoat 被记录为穿在外套里的短款无袖上衣的名字。

items.en: The waistcoat becomes the standard middle layer of the three-piece suit.
items.cn: 马甲成为三件套西装的标准中间层。

items.en: American English calls the same garment a vest, while British English keeps waistcoat.
items.cn: 美式英语把同一件衣服叫 vest，英式英语仍叫 waistcoat。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the two halves of the compound and its close neighbours; the near-meaning group gathers other sleeveless and layered garments.
note.cn: 形近组收复合词的两半与相邻词族；近义组收其它无袖上衣与分层穿着的衣物。

entries.definition: The narrow part of the body between the ribs and the hips; the first half of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「腰」，肋与胯之间的身体部位，是复合词的前一半。

entries.definition: An outer garment with sleeves; the second half of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「外套、上衣」，带袖的外衣，是复合词的后一半。

entries.definition: An underskirt worn under a dress; it shares the coat element but is not a coat.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「衬裙」，同样带 coat 成分，但指的是穿在裙子里的内衣，并非外套。

entries.definition: A heavy coat for cold weather; another coat compound with a different modifier.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「大衣」，另一个 coat 复合词，修饰成分不同。

entries.definition: The American name for the same sleeveless garment; in British English it means an undershirt.
entries.definitionCN: 美式说法，指同一件无袖上衣；在英式英语中它指的是贴身内衣。

entries.definition: A short outer coat with sleeves, worn over the waistcoat.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「短外套、夹克」，带袖，穿在马甲外面。

entries.definition: A sleeveless top with shoulder straps, much less formal than a waistcoat.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「背心式上衣」，带肩带，比马甲随意得多。

entries.definition: A knitted jacket with a buttoned front, warmer and longer than a waistcoat.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「开襟毛衣」，前襟有纽扣，比马甲更暖也更长。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two real words inside the compound and the phrases the garment really appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子利用复合词里两个真实的词，以及这件衣服实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Split it: waist plus coat, a coat that stops at the waist.
normal.cn: 拆开记：waist 加 coat，就是「到腰为止的外套」。

normal.en: The waistcoat is the middle layer of a three-piece suit.
normal.cn: 马甲是三件套西装里的中间那一层。

normal.en: British waiters often wear a black waistcoat over a white shirt.
normal.cn: 英国的服务员常在白衬衫外穿黑色马甲。

normal.en: In the United States the same garment is simply called a vest.
normal.cn: 在美国，同一件衣服直接叫 vest。

normal.en: Compare coat, jacket and cardigan: the waistcoat has no sleeves at all.
normal.cn: 对比 coat、jacket 与 cardigan：马甲完全没有袖子。

abstract.en: Picture a tailor marking a line exactly at the waist and cutting the coat there.
abstract.cn: 想象裁缝在腰间画一条线，就在那里把外套剪断。

abstract.en: Imagine three layers stacked on a chair: shirt, waistcoat, jacket.
abstract.cn: 想象椅子上叠着三层：衬衫、马甲、外套。

abstract.en: Think of a shepherd in a thick knitted waistcoat walking into the snow.
abstract.cn: 想象牧羊人穿着厚针织背心走进雪地。

examples.en: He wore a dark waistcoat over a white shirt.
examples.cn: 他在白衬衫外穿了一件深色马甲。

examples.en: The tailor cut the waistcoat to match the jacket lining.
examples.cn: 裁缝把马甲裁得与外套内衬相配。

examples.en: In British shops the waistcoat is a separate item, not part of the jacket.
examples.cn: 在英国商店里，马甲是单卖的一件，并不附在外套上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「位似扣特」——位于胸前的一件小衣服，扣子特别多：马甲

root: 英语本土复合词：waist「腰」+ coat「外套」，字面即「到腰部的上衣」，首见于十七世纪；它不是拉丁或希腊词根词，核心义由「裁剪到腰」这一服装做法而来。

sensesIntro.en: Waistcoat means one sleeveless inner garment, then the same garment in ceremonial dress, the same thing under its American name, and finally its knitted winter version.
sensesIntro.cn: waistcoat 先指一件无袖内穿衣服，再指礼服中的这件衣服、它在美式英语中的同名物，最后是针织保暖的那一款。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tailors line at the waist, where a short sleeveless layer takes the place of a full coat.
core.cn: 核心意象：裁缝在腰间画的那条线，一件短款无袖上层取代了整件外套。

branches.en: The sleeveless inner garment is the basic clothing sense.
branches.cn: 无袖内穿上衣是基本的服装义。

branches.en: Formal dress fixes the colour and cut of the middle layer.
branches.cn: 礼服规范了中间层的颜色与剪裁。

branches.en: The American name marks the same garment on the other shore.
branches.cn: 美式叫法标记了大西洋对岸的同一件衣服。

branches.en: Knitwear borrows the short waist cut for warmth.
branches.cn: 针织衫借用了「截到腰部」的短款来保暖。

branches.en: A tailored waistcoat and a knitted one share the short protective layer.
branches.cn: 裁缝马甲与针织背心共享「短款保暖层」这一特点。

intro.en: Waistcoat is a plain English compound, so the family gathers its two halves and the words that grew from them.
intro.cn: waistcoat 是朴素的英语复合词，围绕它集合的两半构件与由此长出的词构成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Neither half is Latin: waist is native English and coat came from Old French, so this list holds only non-Latin relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词两半都不是拉丁语：waist 是英语本族词，coat 来自古法语，因此这里没有拉丁同源词。

items.meaning: the narrow part of the body
items.example: Waist sets the length of the garment.
items.exampleCN: waist 决定了这件衣服的长度。

items.example: Coat names the outer garment.
items.exampleCN: coat 指外层的衣服。

items.example: Waistcoat joins the two halves into one garment.
items.exampleCN: waistcoat 把两半合成一件衣服。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms waistcoated.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 waistcoated。

items.example: Waistcoated describes a formally dressed style.
items.exampleCN: waistcoated 描述穿着正式的样式。

items.meaning: material for, or the act of
items.meaningCN: 表材料或动作名词的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ing forms waistcoating.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 waistcoating。

items.example: Waistcoating names the fabric of this garment.
items.exampleCN: waistcoating 指做马甲用的面料。

items.example: Overcoat shows another coat compound.
items.exampleCN: overcoat 是另一个 coat 复合词。

items.example: Petticoat is a second coat compound with an inner sense.
items.exampleCN: petticoat 同样带 coat 构件，却指内层衣物。

definition_zh: 海象
definition_en: a large sea mammal of the Arctic, with thick skin and two long ivory tusks
core_image: 浮冰上一头巨大的海象，嘴边垂着两根白色长牙
scene: 极地的浮冰上，一头巨大的海象正用长牙把身体拖上冰面。On the frozen sea, a huge walrus hauled its heavy body onto the ice with its tusks.
sceneCN: 这里 walrus 是「海象」（第 1 个义项：北极海域的大型海生哺乳动物，有长牙和厚皮）；句意：在结冰的海面上，一头巨大的海象用长牙把笨重的身体拖上了冰面。

derivatives.zh: 由 walrus 加 like 构成，义为「像海象一样的」，常形容浓密的胡须
口语俚语，指集体趴在冰上或岸上晒太阳的行为，由动物的习性引申而来

senses.title: The Arctic sea mammal
senses.definition: a large sea mammal living in the Arctic, with flippers, a thick hide, and two long tusks
senses.definitionCN: 生活在北极海域的大型海生哺乳动物，有鳍状肢、厚皮和两根长牙
senses.example: Walruses rest together on the packed ice.
senses.exampleCN: 海象们一起在密实的浮冰上休息。
senses.why: The word names the animal itself, the creature whose tusks and bulk first caught the eye of northern sailors.
senses.whyCN: 这个词首先指动物本身，即最早被北方水手注意到的长牙、厚皮大家伙。

senses.title: The species as a collective
senses.definition: the whole species or population of walruses, usually discussed in conservation and hunting contexts
senses.definitionCN: 把海象作为一个整体物种来看，多用于保护与捕猎的语境
senses.example: The walrus was hunted for its oil and hide.
senses.exampleCN: 海象曾因取油和兽皮而被捕猎。
senses.why: Once a single animal, the word is used for the whole species when people discuss numbers, hunting, and protection.
senses.whyCN: 从指个体扩展到指整个物种：人们谈数量、捕猎和保护时，海象就成了一个整体的类别。

senses.title: The walrus moustache
senses.definition: a long, thick moustache hanging down at the sides like a walrus tusk
senses.definitionCN: 两侧长而浓密、向下垂的胡子，形似海象的长牙
senses.example: The old captain had a grey walrus moustache.
senses.exampleCN: 老船长长着一把灰白的海象式浓须。
senses.why: The animal gives the image: two drooping tusks turn into the tips of a heavy moustache.
senses.whyCN: 动物的形象被挪用到人身上：两根下垂长牙变成了浓密胡须的两端。

senses.title: Ivory from tusks
senses.definition: walrus ivory, the hard white material cut from the tusks of the animal
senses.definitionCN: 海象牙，从海象长牙上取得的坚硬白色材料
senses.example: Carvers once worked walrus ivory into small figures.
senses.exampleCN: 雕刻师曾把海象牙雕成小雕像。
senses.why: The most striking part of the animal, its tusks, gave the material sense used in trade and carving.
senses.whyCN: 动物身上最醒目的长牙成了贸易与雕刻中的材料义，这一点延续了「以突出部位代整体」的转喻。

senses.title: A clumsy heavy person
senses.definition: a person seen as very large and slow, slightly mocking
senses.definitionCN: 被看作体型庞大、动作迟缓的人，带一点打趣意味
senses.example: The coach called the exhausted swimmer a walrus.
senses.exampleCN: 教练把累坏了的游泳选手叫作海象。
senses.why: The bulk and slowness of the animal produce a playful human label.
senses.whyCN: 海象的庞大与迟缓，被拿来打趣形容人，是从物到人的比喻扩展。

senses.title: A sunbathing group
senses.definition: a joking name for a crowd of people lying together in the sun
senses.definitionCN: 戏称一群并排躺在阳光下暴晒的人
senses.example: Half the beach was a walrus heap that afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 那天下午，半个海滩都是躺成一堆晒太阳的人。
senses.why: Walruses huddle on the ice, so a sunbathing crowd borrows the same picture.
senses.whyCN: 海象爱成群趴在冰上，于是并排暴晒的人群就借用了同一幅画面。

intro.en: Walrus reached English from Dutch, and behind it lies a chain of northern words whose exact origin is still debated.
intro.cn: walrus 经由荷兰语进入英语，其背后是一串北方语言的词形，确切来源仍有争论。

items.en: Early records write morsus rostrum, Latin words for a biting snout, probably a foreign name reshaped into something Latin-like.
items.cn: 早期记录写作 morsus rostrum，拉丁语意为「咬人的嘴」，很可能是把外来名称改写成拉丁语样子的结果。

items.en: Dutch sailors use walvis and later walros, mixing whale and the northern name for the animal.
items.cn: 荷兰水手使用 walvis，后来又出现 walros，把「鲸」和北方语言中对该动物的称呼混在一起。

items.en: The second element probably reflects an Old Norse word hose, while the first is more debated; some connect it to a source meaning whale horse.
items.cn: 后半部分可能对应古诺斯语的 hose（马），前半部分争议更大；有人认为前身意为「鲸马」。

items.en: English adopts walrus, and its spelling is settled during the 1600s.
items.cn: 英语采纳 walrus，拼写在十七世纪逐渐定型。

items.en: The word moves from hunter accounts into ecology and materials such as walrus ivory.
items.cn: 这个词从猎人的叙述进入生态学，也进入「海象牙」等材料描述中。

note.en: Walrus belongs to the Arctic sea beasts, near the whale and the seal in spelling and in habitat.
note.cn: walrus 属于北极海兽，与 whale 拼写相近，与 seal 同处一片栖息地。

entries.definition: Dutch for whale, one probable early source of the English word
entries.definitionCN: 荷兰语中的「鲸」，是英语该词可能的早期来源之一

entries.definition: a very large sea mammal
entries.definitionCN: 鲸；只是拼写与 walrus 相近，词源上两词各自成源

entries.definition: a ridge on cloth, or a weal
entries.definitionCN: 织物上的凸纹；只是拼写与 walrus 前半相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a sea mammal that lives near cold coasts
entries.definitionCN: 海豹；同属北极海兽的常见近邻

entries.definition: a sea mammal with small external ears
entries.definitionCN: 海狮；与海象同为鳍足类动物

entries.definition: the great body of salt water
entries.definitionCN: 海冰；海象主要栖息的地面

normalIntro.en: Walrus carries the tusk and the ice: a heavy northern beast named by sailors.
normalIntro.cn: walrus 带着长牙与浮冰：一种由水手命名的北方巨兽。

normal.en: Walrus comes into English from Dutch, a sailors and traders route.
normal.cn: walrus 经荷兰语进入英语，走的是水手与商人路线。

normal.en: The plural is walruses, not walrus.
normal.cn: 复数是 walruses，而不是 walrus。

normal.en: A walrus moustache is long and drooping like tusks.
normal.cn: walrus moustache 指像长牙一样下垂的浓密胡须。

normal.en: Walrus ivory was carved into small figures.
normal.cn: walrus ivory 指海象牙，曾被雕成小雕像。

normal.en: Compare seal: both live in cold seas, but only the walrus has tusks.
normal.cn: 对比 seal：两者都生活在寒冷海域，但只有海象有长牙。

abstract.en: Picture two white tusks hauling a huge body onto the ice.
abstract.cn: 想象两根白色长牙把庞大的身体拖上冰面。

abstract.en: Imagine a sleeping herd of round bodies packed on drift ice.
abstract.cn: 想象一群圆滚滚的身体挤在浮冰上打盹。

abstract.en: Think of an old captain with a drooping grey moustache.
abstract.cn: 想象一位老船长，灰色的胡子向下垂着。

examples.en: A small group of walruses rested on the drifting ice.
examples.cn: 一小群海象在漂流的浮冰上休息。

examples.en: Hunters long valued walrus tusks as a kind of ivory.
examples.cn: 猎人长期以来把海象长牙当作一种象牙。

examples.en: The old sailor had a broad face and a walrus moustache.
examples.cn: 那位老水手脸膛宽阔，还留着一把海象式浓须。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我拉死」——海象体重大，用长牙拖着身体上冰，好像拉得很费劲；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为经荷兰语 walros 进入英语，后半对应北欧语 hose（马），前半有「鲸」等多说，确切来源存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Walrus starts with the animal, spreads to its species and tusks, and ends in playful human comparisons.
sensesIntro.cn: walrus 从动物本身出发，扩展到物种与长牙，最后延伸为对人的打趣比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tusked sea beast on the ice.
core.cn: 核心意象：浮冰上长着长牙的海兽。

branches.en: The animal itself is the first sense.
branches.cn: 动物本身是第一个义项。

branches.en: The species sense is used for numbers and protection.
branches.cn: 物种义用于数量和保护议题。

branches.en: The moustache sense borrows the drooping tusks.
branches.cn: 浓须义借用了下垂的长牙形象。

branches.en: Ivory comes from the animal most striking part.
branches.cn: 象牙义来自动物最醒目的部位。

branches.en: Both human uses borrow the bulk and the sunbathing herd.
branches.cn: 两个比喻用法分别借来庞大的体型与晒太阳的群体。

intro.en: Walrus is a compound name from northern trading routes; English builds walrus ivory and walrus moustache on it.
intro.cn: walrus 是北方贸易路线传来的复合名称，英语在它之上构成 walrus ivory 与 walrus moustache。

latinIntro.en: No Latin lineage is certain; only an early Latin-looking form morsus rostrum survives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语血脉并不确定，只留下一个早期拉丁化写法 morsus rostrum。

items.example: The first part probably comes from a whale word.
items.exampleCN: 词首部分很可能来自表示「鲸」的词。

items.meaning: possibly horse, as in Old Norse hose
items.example: The ending may echo a northern word for horse.
items.exampleCN: 词尾可能呼应北方语中表示「马」的词。

items.example: The plural -us forms walruses.
items.exampleCN: 复数词尾 -us 构成 walruses。

items.example: The suffix -like forms walruslike.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -like 构成 walruslike。

items.example: The suffix -ing appears in the slang walrusing.
items.exampleCN: 俚语 walrusing 中可见 -ing。

items.example: Tusk is the animal most famous feature in words.
items.exampleCN: tusk 是这种动物在词语中最著名的特征。

items.meaning: the hard white material from tusks
items.example: Ivory pairs with walrus in trade names.
items.exampleCN: ivory 与 walrus 组合成贸易名称。

items.example: Moustache pairs with walrus in a fixed phrase.
items.exampleCN: moustache 与 walrus 组成固定短语。

items.example: Herd gives a herd of walruses.
items.exampleCN: herd 构成 a herd of walruses。

definition_zh: 授权令；拘票；正当理由；保证；使有必要
definition_en: an official document giving power to act, or a good reason that makes an action right
core_image: 法官在纸上盖章签发一张许可文书
scene: 警方带着搜查证来到仓库门口。The police arrived at the warehouse door with a search warrant.
sceneCN: 这里 warrant 是「授权令、搜查证」（第 3 个义项：官方签发的授权文书）；句意：警方拿着一份搜查证来到仓库门口。

derivatives.zh: 由 warrant 加词尾 -y 构成，义为「保证书；保修单」
由动词加 -ed 构成，义为「有正当理由的；有保证的」
由 un- 加 warranted 构成，义为「无正当理由的；无端的」

senses.title: To justify or make necessary
senses.definition: to give enough reason for something to be done or to deserve attention
senses.definitionCN: 为做某事提供足够理由，或值得被注意
senses.example: The damage does not warrant a full refund.
senses.exampleCN: 这点损坏还不至于要求全额退款。
senses.why: The core image is a sealed paper that makes an act lawful, so to warrant is to give something its best reason.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一张盖章文书让行为合法，因此动词意为「为某事提供最正当的理由」。

senses.title: To guarantee
senses.definition: to promise formally that something is true or will happen
senses.definitionCN: 正式承诺某事为真或将会发生
senses.example: I warrant you will find the book useful.
senses.exampleCN: 我保证你会发现这本书有用。
senses.why: A warrant in law stands for the truth of a claim, which gives the old promise sense.
senses.whyCN: 法律上的担保文书为一项说法背书，于是动词发展出「保证」的意思。

senses.title: An official authorising document
senses.definition: a written order from a court or authority giving someone power to act
senses.definitionCN: 法院或当局签发的书面命令，给予某人采取行动的权力
senses.example: Officers seized the documents under a warrant.
senses.exampleCN: 警员凭一份搜查令取走了这些文件。
senses.why: The paper with a seal is the most concrete sense: it grants the right to enter, search, or arrest.
senses.whyCN: 盖章的纸张是最具体的义项：它授人以进入、搜查或逮捕的权力。

senses.title: A court warrant for arrest
senses.definition: a legal document authorising arrest or for bringing a person before a court
senses.definitionCN: 授权逮捕或将某人带至法庭的法律文书
senses.example: A warrant was issued for his arrest.
senses.exampleCN: 针对他的逮捕令已经发出。
senses.why: Narrowed usage: the same authority paper now names the arrest order in headlines.
senses.whyCN: 用法收窄：同样的授权文书，现在常见于新闻中以「逮捕令」的身份出现。

senses.title: Good reason
senses.definition: a sound reason that supports an action or belief
senses.definitionCN: 支持某种行动或信念的充分理由
senses.example: There is no warrant for such anger.
senses.exampleCN: 这样的愤怒没有正当理由。
senses.why: Drop the paper and only its force remains: warrant becomes a synonym for justification.
senses.whyCN: 去掉文书本身，只剩它的效力，「warrant」于是成为「正当理由」的同义词。

senses.title: A promise of quality
senses.definition: an assurance that a product or claim meets a stated standard
senses.definitionCN: 对产品或说法符合既定标准的保证
senses.example: The warrant covers repairs for one year.
senses.exampleCN: 这份质量保证涵盖为期一年的维修。
senses.why: Merchants sealed their word of quality with a warrant; modern warranties inherit this sense.
senses.whyCN: 旧时商人用文书为自己的质量承诺盖章，现代保修单就继承了这个义项。

intro.en: Warrant comes from Old Northern French warant and ultimately from a Germanic root meaning to defend or protect.
intro.cn: warrant 来自古北部法语 warant，最终源于日耳曼语中意为「保护、护卫」的词根。

items.en: A protective Germanic form gives the sense of defending or vouching for someone.
items.cn: 日耳曼语的保护类词形带来了「为某人担保、护卫」的意味。

items.en: Warant means a guarantee or a protector.
items.cn: 古法语 warant 意为保证或保护者。

items.en: Warrant enters law as a document that entitles a person to act.
items.cn: warrant 以「授予某人行动权的文书」进入法律英语。

items.en: The verb sense to justify and the noun sense of good reason develop.
items.cn: 动词「使之合理」和名词「正当理由」两个义项在这一时期发展出来。

items.en: Warranty splits off as a separate noun for products and promises.
items.cn: warranty 分离出去，专门表示产品的保证与承诺。

note.en: Warrant overlaps with guarantee in law and trade, and with authorize in everyday use.
note.cn: warrant 在法律与贸易语境中与 guarantee 重叠，在日常用法中则靠近 authorize。

entries.definition: a written promise about a product
entries.definitionCN: 产品保修单；与 warrant 同出一源

entries.definition: justified, or covered by a guarantee
entries.definitionCN: 有正当理由的；有保证的

entries.definition: a person who gives a guarantee
entries.definitionCN: 担保人；由 warrant 加 -or 派生

entries.definition: a formal promise that something will happen
entries.definitionCN: 担保；保证

entries.definition: to give official permission
entries.definitionCN: 授权；批准

entries.definition: to give a good reason for something
entries.definitionCN: 证明……正当

normalIntro.en: Warrant is the sealed paper of the old law: it grants a right and then becomes a reason.
normalIntro.cn: warrant 是旧时法律的一张盖章文书：先授予权力，再化为理由。

normal.en: A search warrant lets police enter a place.
normal.cn: search warrant 是允许警方进入某处的搜查令。

normal.en: Warrant the sense of justify is common in formal writing.
normal.cn: warrant 的「使……合理」之义常见于正式写作。

normal.en: Warranty is the product version of the same idea.
normal.cn: warranty 是同一概念在产品上的版本。

normal.en: Unwarranted means without any good reason.
normal.cn: unwarranted 意为没有正当理由的。

normal.en: Compare guarantee: warranty is often narrow and commercial, warrant is legal.
normal.cn: 对比 guarantee：warranty 偏商业，warrant 偏法律。

abstract.en: Picture a judge pressing a red seal onto a paper.
abstract.cn: 想象法官把红色印章按在纸上。

abstract.en: Imagine the paper turning into a thin thread that pulls an action forward.
abstract.cn: 想象纸变成一根细线，把一项行动拉出来。

abstract.en: Think of a shop card promising a free repair.
abstract.cn: 想象一张承诺免费维修的商店卡片。

examples.en: The judge issued a warrant for the missing driver.
examples.cn: 法官对那位失踪的司机签发了逮捕令。

examples.en: Such a small delay hardly warrants a complaint.
examples.cn: 这么小的延误几乎不值得投诉。

examples.en: The raiders entered the house without a warrant.
examples.cn: 那些人没有搜查令就闯进了屋子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我认的」——法官认定之后才签发授权令；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 源自古北部法语 warant（保证、保护者），更早与日耳曼语「护卫」词根同源，核心义为「为一事作担保」。

sensesIntro.en: Warrant moves from the act of justifying, to a sealed order, to a good reason, and finally to commercial promises.
sensesIntro.cn: warrant 从「使……合理」出发，经盖章命令，到「正当理由」，最后到商业保证。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sealed paper that grants a right.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张盖了章、授予权力的纸。

branches.en: To justify is the verb drawn from the paper.
branches.cn: 「使合理」是由文书引申出的动词义。

branches.en: Guaranteeing keeps the old vouching sense.
branches.cn: 「保证」保留了旧时作担保的含义。

branches.en: The warrant as a legal order is the concrete sense.
branches.cn: 作为法律文书的授权令是具体义项。

branches.en: The arrest order narrows the document to one use.
branches.cn: 逮捕令把该文书缩小到一种专门用途。

branches.en: Good reason is the power alone, quality promise is the trade version.
branches.cn: 「正当理由」只保留效力，「质量保证」是商业版本。

intro.en: Warrant is a borrowed root; English grows warranty, warranted, and unwarranted around it.
intro.cn: warrant 是借入词根，英语围绕它构成 warranty、warranted 与 unwarranted。

latinIntro.en: The word is French and Germanic, so Latin carries no direct form; French warant is the nearest ancestor.
latinIntro.cn: 该词来自法语与日耳曼语，拉丁语没有直接形式，最近的祖先是法语 warant。

items.example: Warant is the direct French source.
items.exampleCN: warant 是直接的法语来源。

items.example: The ending -ant shapes the borrowed noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ant 塑造了借入的名词形式。

items.example: The suffix -y forms warranty.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成 warranty。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms warranted.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 warranted。

items.example: The prefix un- forms unwarranted.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unwarranted。

items.example: The suffix -able forms warrantable.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 构成 warrantable。

items.example: Warrantee names the protected side.
items.exampleCN: warrantee 指受担保的一方。

items.meaning: the person who gives a guarantee
items.example: Warrantor names the giving side.
items.exampleCN: warrantor 指作出担保的一方。

items.example: Warrant officer shows the root in official titles.
items.exampleCN: warrant officer 显示词根在官衔中的使用。

latinEntries.example: Guarantia shows the family passing through Latin form.
latinEntries.exampleCN: guarantia 表明这一词族曾以拉丁形式流传。

definition_zh: 浪费；损耗；损耗率
definition_en: the loss of something through waste or through people or goods dropping out
core_image: 木桶底的小缝，细水长流地漏掉一部分东西
scene: 工厂发现原料在加工过程中损耗不少。The factory found considerable wastage of raw material during processing.
sceneCN: 这里 wastage 是「损耗、浪费」（第 1 个义项：因使用不当或流程问题而流失的部分）；句意：工厂发现原料在加工过程中损耗不少。

derivatives.zh: wastage 的基础词，义为「浪费；消耗」
waste 加 -ful 构成，义为「浪费的」
waste 加 -er 构成，义为「浪费者；废品」
waste 加 -ing 构成，义为「消耗性的；使人消瘦的」

senses.title: Loss caused by waste
senses.definition: the amount or the fact of something being wasted
senses.definitionCN: 东西被浪费掉的数量或事实
senses.example: The report measured food wastage in kitchens.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告统计了厨房里的食物浪费。
senses.why: Waste is the verb, and -age turns the act into a noun naming the loss itself.
senses.whyCN: waste 是动词，-age 把动作变成名词，指作为结果存在的损失。

senses.title: Loss of people through leaving
senses.definition: the loss of staff through resignation, retirement, or other ways out of an organisation
senses.definitionCN: 因辞职、退休等离开组织而造成的人员流失
senses.example: The firm relied on natural wastage to cut jobs.
senses.exampleCN: 公司靠自然减员来削减岗位。
senses.why: People leaving are also goods lost, so the same noun covers staff numbers.
senses.whyCN: 人员离开也像货物流失，因此同一个名词被用来指人员数量的减少。

senses.title: The rate of loss
senses.definition: a percentage or figure showing how much is lost over time
senses.definitionCN: 表示一段时间内损失多少的百分比或数字
senses.example: The wastage rate fell after the pipes were fixed.
senses.exampleCN: 修好管道后，损耗率下降了。
senses.why: Once a loss can be counted, the abstract noun becomes a number and takes the sense of a rate.
senses.whyCN: 损失一旦可以计数，名词就从抽象状态变成数字，进而表示比率。

senses.title: Loss in a supplied stock
senses.definition: the loss of stock or supplies between delivery and use
senses.definitionCN: 从交货到使用之间库存或物资的损失
senses.example: Almost no wastage occurred in the warehouse this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年仓库几乎没有出现库存损耗。
senses.why: Commerce takes the general sense and fixes it to stocks that vanish between delivery and use.
senses.whyCN: 商业把一般义固定到「交货到使用之间消失的物资」上，形成库存损耗。

senses.title: Wear or weakening in structure
senses.definition: gradual loss of material or strength in a structure or product over time
senses.definitionCN: 结构或产品在一段时间内逐渐失去材料或强度
senses.example: Engineers checked the bridge for wastage at the joints.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师检查了桥梁节点处的损耗。
senses.why: Slow loss of material from a body fits the image of water leaking through a crack.
senses.whyCN: 物体缓慢失去材料，正对应「水从裂缝漏走」的画面。

intro.en: Wastage is an English formation from waste plus -age, naming the loss itself rather than the act.
intro.cn: wastage 是英语自身构成的新词，由 waste 加 -age 而成，指损失本身而非动作。

items.en: Vastare means to lay waste, and classical Latin vastum means empty or desolate.
items.cn: vastare 意为使荒废，古典拉丁语 vastum 意为空荡、荒凉。

items.en: Waster brings the meaning to waste or ruin into French.
items.cn: 古法语 waster 把「浪费、毁坏」的意思带入法语。

items.en: Waste takes root in English as verb and noun.
items.cn: waste 以动词和名词身份在英语中扎根。

items.en: Wastage first appears, using -age to name a measurable loss.
items.cn: wastage 首次出现，用 -age 词尾表示可计量的损失。

items.en: Factory reports and staff planning adopt the word for materials and for people.
items.cn: 工厂报表与人员规划都用这个词指物料和人员的流失。

note.en: Wastage sits in the waste family, and its nearest neighbours are loss and attrition in staff contexts.
note.cn: wastage 属于 waste 词族，最近邻是 loss 以及人事语境中的 attrition。

entries.definition: to use badly or to lose for nothing
entries.definitionCN: 浪费；使……白费；是 wastage 的基础词

entries.definition: using more than is needed
entries.definitionCN: 浪费的；不节俭的

entries.definition: a person who wastes things
entries.definitionCN: 浪费者；由 waste 加 -er 派生

entries.definition: the fact of losing something
entries.definitionCN: 损失；丧失

entries.definition: gradual reduction of staff
entries.definitionCN: 人员逐渐减少

entries.definition: liquid that escapes and is lost
entries.definitionCN: 洒出或漏掉导致的浪费

normalIntro.en: Wastage is waste turned into a quantity: the -age suffix makes a noun you can count.
normalIntro.cn: wastage 是把 waste 变成一种量：-age 词尾让浪费成为可以计数的名词。

normal.en: Food wastage is a common phrase in reports.
normal.cn: food wastage 是报告中常见的说法。

normal.en: Natural wastage means staff leaving are not replaced.
normal.cn: natural wastage 指人员离职后不再补缺。

normal.en: Wastage is usually uncountable, so no plural is common.
normal.cn: wastage 通常不可数，少见复数。

normal.en: Wastage and wasteful share the same base word.
normal.cn: wastage 与 wasteful 共用同一个基础词。

normal.en: Compare loss: loss is general, wastage stresses avoidable waste.
normal.cn: 对比 loss：loss 更泛，wastage 强调本可避免的浪费。

abstract.en: Picture a bucket leaking drop by drop from a hairline crack.
abstract.cn: 想象一只木桶从细缝里一滴一滴漏水。

abstract.en: Imagine a warehouse shelf where boxes quietly disappear each month.
abstract.cn: 想象仓库货架上的箱子每个月悄悄少一点。

abstract.en: Think of a company where empty desks are never refilled.
abstract.cn: 想象一家公司里空出的座位再也不补人。

examples.en: Water wastage is a serious problem in dry regions.
examples.cn: 在干旱地区，水资源浪费是个严重问题。

examples.en: The company used natural wastage to reduce its staff.
examples.cn: 公司通过自然减员来缩减人员。

examples.en: Better packing cut wastage of fruit in transport.
examples.cn: 改进包装减少了水果在运输中的损耗。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂死他」——把东西一股脑喂进去、喂到死，就是浪费；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语本土构词：waste（浪费，来自拉丁语 vastare 使荒废）加名词词尾 -age（行为或结果），表示被浪费掉的量。

sensesIntro.en: Wastage first names the loss made by waste, then applies it to people, to rates, to stock, and to wear.
sensesIntro.cn: wastage 先指因浪费造成的损失，再延伸到人员、比率、库存与磨损。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small leak that steadily drains what was stored.
core.cn: 核心意象：细小的裂缝持续漏掉储存的东西。

branches.en: Loss through waste is the base sense.
branches.cn: 因浪费而受损失是基础义项。

branches.en: Staff losses borrow the same noun.
branches.cn: 人员流失借用了同一个名词。

branches.en: The rate sense turns the loss into a figure.
branches.cn: 比率义把损失变成数字。

branches.en: Stock loss fixes the word to inventory.
branches.cn: 库存损耗把词固定在存货语境里。

branches.en: Structural wear is the slowest and most physical form of loss.
branches.cn: 结构损耗是损失中最缓慢、最具体的一种。

intro.en: Wastage is built from the English waste and the French-derived suffix -age, with wasteful and waster in the same family.
intro.cn: wastage 由英语 waste 加法语来源的词尾 -age 构成，同族的还有 wasteful 与 waster。

latinIntro.en: Latin vastare, to lay waste, lies behind the waste family and behind French words such as waster.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vastare 意为使荒废，是 waste 词族以及法语 waster 等词的源头。

items.meaning: to use badly or lose for nothing
items.example: Waste is the base of the compound noun.
items.exampleCN: waste 复合名词的基础部分。

items.example: The suffix -age forms wastage.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -age 构成 wastage。

items.example: The suffix -ful forms wasteful.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ful 构成 wasteful。

items.example: The suffix -er forms waster.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 waster。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms wasting.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 wasting。

items.example: Vastare gives the empty and ruined image.
items.exampleCN: vastare 带来了空荡、毁坏的意象。

items.example: Spillage shows the same -age pattern.
items.exampleCN: spillage 展示了同样的 -age 模式。

items.example: Leakage is the closest sister noun.
items.exampleCN: leakage 是最近的同型名词。

items.example: Natural wastage is the most famous collocation.
items.exampleCN: natural wastage 是最著名的搭配。

definition_zh: 水传播的；（货物等）水运的；（化学品等）水溶性的；水上生活的
definition_en: carried by water, especially describing a disease or substance spread through water or carried by boat
core_image: 一个小点被水流托起来，顺水漂向远处的下一个人
scene: 暴雨过后，村里的井水变了颜色，医生挨家挨户发放净水药片。Doctors warned that the outbreak spreading through the village was waterborne.
sceneCN: 这里 waterborne 是「经水传播的」（第 1 个义项：疾病或污染物借水而扩散）；句意是医生警告，村里扩散的这次疫情是经水传播的。画面里能辨认的物件有变色的井水、净水药片和挨家走访的医生。

pos.zh: 形容词：水传播的；水运的；水溶性的；水上生活的；可用 more 与 most 构成比较级

derivatives.zh: borne 是 bear 的过去分词，此处作复合词尾，义为「被承载的；由……携带的」
water 是复合词的第一部分，义为「水」，与 borne 合起来表示「由水携带」
由 air 与 borne 构成，是 waterborne 的同构反衬，义为「空气传播的」
由 blood 与 borne 构成，义为「血液传播的」，与 waterborne 同属传播方式词族
由 food 与 borne 构成，义为「食物传播的」，与 waterborne 并列

senses.title: Carried through water
senses.titleCN: 经水传播的：疾病随水扩散
senses.definition: spread or carried through water, especially of an infectious disease or a contaminant
senses.definitionCN: 通过水传播或携带的，尤指传染病或污染物
senses.example: The village clinic blamed the waterborne infection on a cracked well cover.
senses.exampleCN: 村卫生室把那起经水传播的感染归咎于一口破裂的井盖。
senses.why: The verb bear means to carry, and its past participle borne supplies the second half of the compound, so waterborne literally describes something carried by water.
senses.whyCN: 动词 bear 意为「承载」，它的过去分词 borne 构成复合词的后半部分，所以 waterborne 字面就是「被水带着的」，经水传播是这个意象最直接的引申。

senses.title: Carried by boat or ship
senses.definition: transported by boat or ship rather than by road or rail
senses.definitionCN: 靠船或轮船而非公路、铁路运输的
senses.example: Most of the island supplies are waterborne and arrive by barge.
senses.exampleCN: 岛上大部分物资靠水运，由驳船运到。
senses.why: The same carrying idea moves from microbes to goods: anything a hull can hold and float from port to port is waterborne.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「承载」意象从病菌移到货物上：凡是船舱能装、能从一个港口漂到另一个港口的，就是水运的。

senses.title: Dissolved or dispersed in water
senses.titleCN: 水溶性的：溶解或分散在水里的
senses.definition: dissolved, suspended, or carried in water, as in paints and chemicals
senses.definitionCN: 溶解、悬浮或由水携带的，如涂料和化学品
senses.example: Waterborne paints dry faster and release less solvent into the air.
senses.exampleCN: 水性涂料干得更快，向空气中释放的溶剂也更少。
senses.why: In industry the carrier is a liquid: a medium that holds a substance, which is the same image reduced to chemistry.
senses.whyCN: 在工业语境里，承载体变成了一种液体：它装着某样物质，这正是同一意象在化学层面的缩小版。

senses.title: Existing or living on the water
senses.titleCN: 水上生活的；以水面为基础的
senses.definition: existing, living, or taking place on the surface of water
senses.definitionCN: 存在于、生活于或发生在水面之上的
senses.example: These waterborne creatures feed close to the surface at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 这些栖居水面的生物在黄昏时靠近表层觅食。
senses.why: If water can carry a thing, that thing can live on water; a whole lifestyle can be waterborne.
senses.whyCN: 既然水能承载某样东西，那样东西就可以以水为家；一整套生活方式也可以建在水上。

intro.en: Waterborne is an English compound of water and borne, the past participle of bear, so it names whatever is carried by water.
intro.cn: waterborne 是英语本土复合词，由 water 与 borne 组成，borne 是 bear 的过去分词，整个词指「被水承载的东西」。

items.en: The ancestor of bear is reconstructed as *beran, meaning to carry or bring.
items.cn: bear 的祖先是重构形式 *beran，一般认为意为「携带、带来」。

items.en: In Old English the verb beran already meant to carry, and to bring forth.
items.cn: 在古英语中，动词 beran 已经兼有「携带」与「生育」两个意思。

items.en: Middle English used boren and borne as the past participle while the verb form was still settling.
items.cn: 中古英语的过去分词写作 boren 或 borne，当时动词形式尚未完全固定。

items.en: English regularly joins a noun with a past participle: water plus borne makes a compact description of carriage.
items.cn: 英语常用名词加过去分词构词：water 与 borne 合在一起，简洁地描述「被承载」这件事。

items.en: The adjective appears in sailing and trade writing first, describing goods moved by boat rather than by road.
items.cn: 这个形容词最早出现在航海与贸易文本中，用来描述靠船而非陆路运输的货物。

items.en: Public health writing later applied the same word to diseases whose germs travel in water.
items.cn: 后来公共卫生文献把这个词用到病菌随水传播的疾病上。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the other -borne compounds; the near-meaning group gathers words about water, sickness and transport.
note.cn: 形近组收其他以 borne 结尾的复合词；近义组收关于水、疾病与运输的词。

entries.definition: Carried through the air, especially of diseases, seeds or dust; built exactly like waterborne.
entries.definitionCN: 经空气传播的，尤指疾病、种子或灰尘；构词方式与 waterborne 完全相同。

entries.definition: The past participle of bear, meaning carried; it is the back half of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: bear 的过去分词，意为「被携带的」；它就是本复合词的后半部分。

entries.definition: Carried through blood, as of viruses and other pathogens.
entries.definitionCN: 经血液传播的，如病毒等病原体。

entries.definition: Carried through food, as of bacteria and toxins.
entries.definitionCN: 经食物传播的，如细菌和毒素。

entries.definition: Relating to giving birth, from the other sense of bear; it looks related but means something else.
entries.definitionCN: 与生育有关的，取自 bear 的另一义「生育」；拼写相似，含义不同。

entries.definition: Containing or made of water; a technical adjective for solutions, not for transmission.
entries.definitionCN: 含水的、水制的；属于技术用语，用于溶液，不用于描述传播方式。

entries.definition: Spreading by contact between people, without saying through what medium.
entries.definitionCN: 靠人与人接触传播的，不说明借什么媒介扩散。

entries.definition: Able to be passed from one person or organism to another; wider than waterborne.
entries.definitionCN: 能从一个个体传给另一个个体的；比 waterborne 范围更宽。

entries.definition: Sent by ship or other transport; the plain verb with no hint of water as carrier.
entries.definitionCN: 用船或其他方式运出的；普通动词，不暗示水是载体。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real parts of the compound: water plus borne, the past participle of bear.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用这个复合词的真实成分：water 加上 bear 的过去分词 borne。

normal.en: Borne is the past participle of bear, so waterborne means carried by water.
normal.cn: borne 是 bear 的过去分词，所以 waterborne 就是「被水承载的」。

normal.en: Airborne, bloodborne and foodborne are built the same way, with a different carrier in front.
normal.cn: airborne、bloodborne、foodborne 的构词方式相同，只是前面的载体不同。

normal.en: A waterborne disease is one whose germs ride in drinking water.
normal.cn: waterborne disease 指病菌随着饮用水传播的疾病。

normal.en: Waterborne trade is trade carried on the water, not on the road.
normal.cn: waterborne trade 是指在水中进行的贸易，而不是陆路上的贸易。

normal.en: Waterborne paint uses water as its carrier instead of a solvent.
normal.cn: waterborne paint 用水作载体，而不用溶剂。

abstract.en: Picture a single dot lifted by a stream and dropped far downstream.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小点被水流托起，落在很远的下游。

abstract.en: Imagine a barge loaded to the rail, floating goods from island to island.
abstract.cn: 想象一艘装到船舷的驳船，在岛屿之间漂浮着运送货物。

abstract.en: Think of a brush dipped in water, the colour spreading as the water carries it.
abstract.cn: 想象一支蘸了水的画笔，颜色随着水四处散开。

examples.en: The relief team tests every well to rule out waterborne illness.
examples.cn: 救援队检测每一口井，以排除水源性疾病的可能。

examples.en: The old city grew rich on the waterborne trade of the delta.
examples.cn: 这座古城因三角洲的水上贸易而富庶起来。

examples.en: Switching to a waterborne varnish cut the factory odour complaints by half.
examples.cn: 改用水性清漆后，工厂的异味投诉减少了一半。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「窝特邦」——特邦的水流把病菌一路带到下游；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语本土复合词：water（水，古英语 wæter）+ borne（bear 的过去分词，意为「被携带的」）。bear 可上溯到重构形式 *beran「携带」；两半合起来即「被水承载的」，先用于水运，后用于水媒传播。

sensesIntro.en: The four senses all extend the same carrying image: a germ, a cargo, a pigment and a creature are each held up by water.
