sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项都在延伸同一个「承载」意象：病菌、货物、颜料与生物，先后被水托着带走。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small dot is lifted by the current and carried downriver.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个小点被水流托起，被带向下游。

branches.en: CONTAGION: germs travelling in drinking water make the disease waterborne.
branches.cn: 传染线：病菌随饮用水传播，疾病便成为经水传播的。

branches.en: CARGO: goods that a hull carries from port to port are waterborne goods.
branches.cn: 货载线：由船从一个港口运到另一个港口的，是水运货物。

branches.en: MEDIUM: a liquid that holds a substance is the same carrier idea in chemistry.
branches.cn: 介质线：液体承载物质，是同一承载意象在化学中的表现。

branches.en: HOME: a creature that lives on the water surface is carried by it every day.
branches.cn: 栖居线：日日夜夜以水面为家的生物，始终由水承载。

branches.en: Both the germ and the cargo depend on one moved thing and one moving medium.
branches.cn: 病菌与货物都依赖「一样被搬动的东西」加「一种流动的媒介」。

intro.en: Waterborne is a native English compound, so its parts are ordinary English words rather than Latin roots.
intro.cn: waterborne 是英语本土复合词，组成部分是普通英语词，而不是拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for waterborne; Latin aqua, water, and ferre, to carry, are only meaning neighbours.
latinIntro.cn: waterborne 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 aqua（水）与 ferre（搬运）只是意思相近的邻词。

items.example: The first element names the carrier.
items.exampleCN: 第一个成分点明载体是水。

items.example: The second element says how the thing is carried.
items.exampleCN: 第二个成分说明东西是怎么被带的。

items.example: The participle borne comes from this verb.
items.exampleCN: borne 这个过去分词就来自这个动词。

items.example: The ending marks the past participle form.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标明过去分词形式。

items.example: Airborne is built in the same pattern.
items.exampleCN: airborne 按同样的模式构成。

items.example: Bloodborne swaps water for blood.
items.exampleCN: bloodborne 把 water 换成了 blood。

items.example: Foodborne uses a third carrier.
items.exampleCN: foodborne 用了第三种载体。

items.meaningCN: 被水承载的；经水传播的
items.example: The full word names the product.
items.exampleCN: 整个词指明被水承载的结果。

definition_zh: 滨海区；水边；临水的地带；码头区
definition_en: the part of a town or city that runs along the edge of water, especially one with docks or a promenade
core_image: 一条街道紧贴着水面铺开，房子背靠城里、正面朝江
scene: 傍晚的江边，散步的人沿着栏杆慢慢走，旧仓库改成了咖啡馆。In the evening the waterfront is full of families watching the ferries come in.
sceneCN: 这里 waterfront 是「临水地带、滨水区」（第 1 个义项：城镇紧挨水边的区域）；句意是傍晚时滨水区到处都是看渡轮进港的家庭。画面里能辨认的物件有江边栏杆、改作咖啡馆的旧仓库和进港的渡轮。

pos.zh: 名词：滨水区；水边；码头区；滨海地带
形容词：滨水区的；位于水边的（多作定语，如 waterfront development）

derivatives.zh: 复合词第一部分，义为「水」，与 front 合起来表示「朝水的一侧」
复合词第二部分，义为「正面；面向」，指建筑或街道朝向的那一面
复数形式，义为「多处滨水地带」，指一个地方的多片临水区域
由 sea 与 front 构成的同构复合词，义为「海滨区」
由 river 与 front 构成，义为「河畔区」，与 waterfront 同属几类水岸词

senses.title: The part of a city facing the water
senses.titleCN: 滨水区：城市临水的一片地区
senses.definition: the area of a town or city that lies along the edge of a sea, river, lake or harbour
senses.definitionCN: 城镇或城市濒临海洋、河流、湖泊或港湾的一片区域
senses.example: The city rebuilt its waterfront with a park, a museum and a long promenade.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市重建了滨水区，建起公园、博物馆和一条长长的步行道。
senses.why: Front means the face of a building or a body that looks outward, so the waterfront is the side of a town that turns to the water.
senses.whyCN: front 指建筑或身体朝外的那一面，所以 waterfront 就是城镇转向水的那一侧。

senses.title: An area with docks and port activity
senses.titleCN: 码头区：带有船坞、装卸与贸易的区域
senses.definition: a harbour fringe with wharves, warehouses and the traffic of ships and cargo
senses.definitionCN: 港湾边缘设有码头、仓库并有大船与货物往来的地方
senses.example: Sailors used to find cheap rooms on the waterfront near the old docks.
senses.exampleCN: 水手过去常能在旧码头附近的码头区找到便宜的房间。
senses.why: Where there is a face turned to the water, ships come and go, so the word also names the working docks along that edge.
senses.whyCN: 凡是转向水的那一侧，就有船只往来，于是这个词也指紧贴这条边缘的作业码头区。

senses.title: Water frontage of land or a building
senses.titleCN: 临水正面：土地或建筑直接面对水的那一面
senses.definition: the stretch of a property or building that directly faces the water and often gives a clear view of it
senses.definitionCN: 财产或建筑直接朝向水面、常能取得开阔水景的那一段
senses.example: The cabin has a wide waterfront with a private jetty.
senses.exampleCN: 这间小屋临水正面很宽，还带一个私家小码头。
senses.why: Of a single property, front means the side that faces the water, so only one plot has its own waterfront.
senses.whyCN: 就一处产业而言，front 指朝向水的那一面，所以一块土地便有了自己的临水正面。

senses.title: Capitalized name of a street or district
senses.titleCN: 专名：滨水区一带的街道或地段名
senses.definition: as a capitalized name, the proper name of a road, park or neighbourhood beside water
senses.definitionCN: 首字母大写时，指水边道路、公园或街区的专有名称
senses.example: The orchestra played all summer at the Waterfront in the old harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 整个夏天，管弦乐队都在老港口的滨水区演出。
senses.why: A familiar strip of land is often named plainly, so the compound is capitalized as the name of the place itself.
senses.whyCN: 一片人们熟悉的地带常常被直接拿来命名，于是这个复合词首字母大写，成为该地点的名称。

intro.en: Waterfront joins the two native English words water and front, and the compound is recorded in English trade writing.
intro.cn: waterfront 由英语本土词 water 与 front 组合而成，这个复合词见于英语贸易文本。

items.en: Water goes back to Old English wæter, a word shared by all the Germanic languages.
items.cn: water 可上溯到古英语 wæter，这是各日耳曼语言共有的词。

items.en: Front comes through Old French from Latin frons, the forehead or the face of a building.
items.cn: front 经由古法语来自拉丁语 frons，本义是「前额」或建筑的正面。

items.en: By the late Middle Ages franunten and front were in English for the face and the forward side.
items.cn: 到中世纪末，front 已经出现在英语里，指面部和朝前的一侧。

items.en: Trade and port writing joined water and front to mark the strip of land that meets the tide.
items.cn: 十七、十八世纪的贸易与港口文献把 water 与 front 组合起来，指与潮水相接的那一条土地。

items.en: Nineteenth-century port cities spoke of the waterfront as the working docks, and the twentieth century added a leisure sense with promenades and parks.
items.cn: 十九世纪的港口城市用 waterfront 指作业码头，二十世纪则增添了带步行道与公园的休闲含义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other compounds for the edge of the water; the near-meaning group gathers port and shore words with a different focus.
note.cn: 形近组收其他表示水边的复合词；近义组收重点不同的港口与海岸词。

entries.definition: The forward or outward face of something; the second half of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的正面或朝外的一面；就是这个复合词的后半部分。

entries.definition: The land along a river, built exactly like waterfront with river in front.
entries.definitionCN: 沿河的土地，构词方式与 waterfront 完全相同，只是前面换成了 river。

entries.definition: The section of a coastal town that faces the open sea, often with a promenade.
entries.definitionCN: 海边城镇面对开阔大海的部分，常有步行道。

entries.definition: A property or strip of land directly on a beach.
entries.definitionCN: 直接临海滩的房产或土地。

entries.definition: The shore strip of a lake, usually with houses or parks.
entries.definitionCN: 湖滨地带，通常有房屋或公园。

entries.definition: The structures where ships load and unload; the working part of a waterfront.
entries.definitionCN: 船只装卸货物的设施；滨水区中作业的部分。

entries.definition: A sheltered stretch of water where ships can stay safe; the water itself, not the town edge.
entries.definitionCN: 船只可以安全停泊的受庇护水域；指的是水本身，而不是城镇边缘。

entries.definition: A landing place built along the water for loading and unloading.
entries.definitionCN: 沿水修建、用于装卸货物的码头平台。

entries.definition: A public walk, often beside the sea; a leisure feature of many waterfronts.
entries.definitionCN: 公共散步道，常在海边；是许多滨水区的休闲设施。

entries.definition: The whole line where land meets the sea; far wider than one town waterfront.
entries.definitionCN: 陆地与海相接的整条线；比一座城镇的滨水区大得多。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real parts of the compound and the phrases it appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用这个复合词的真实成分，以及它实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Front is the face that looks outward, so waterfront is the face of a town turned toward water.
normal.cn: front 是朝外的脸，所以 waterfront 就是城镇转向水的那张脸。

normal.en: Water plus front makes the same pattern as seafront and riverfront.
normal.cn: water 加 front 与 seafront、riverfront 用的是同一个模式。

normal.en: On the waterfront is the usual phrase for the strip of land along the harbour.
normal.cn: on the waterfront 是描述沿港那一条土地的常用说法。

normal.en: Waterfront property sells for more because it faces open water.
normal.cn: waterfront property 价格更高，就因为它直接面对开阔水面。

normal.en: A waterfront development turns old docks into homes, shops and parks.
normal.cn: waterfront development 把旧码头改造成住宅、商店和公园。

abstract.en: Picture a row of houses with their backs to the hills and their fronts to the river.
abstract.cn: 想象一排房子背靠小山，正面朝着江面。

abstract.en: Imagine a long railing where children lean out to watch the ferries.
abstract.cn: 想象一道长栏杆，孩子们趴在上面看渡轮。

abstract.en: Think of old cranes beside new cafés, one strip of land holding both.
abstract.cn: 想象旧吊车旁边就是新咖啡馆，同一条土地同时容纳两者。

examples.en: The new museum was built on the waterfront beside the old cranes.
examples.cn: 新博物馆建在旧吊车旁的滨水区。

examples.en: Families stroll along the waterfront on summer evenings.
examples.cn: 夏日的傍晚，一家人沿着滨水区散步。

examples.en: Plans to redevelop the waterfront met strong local opposition.
examples.cn: 重新开发滨水区的计划遭到了当地人的强烈反对。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「窝特弗兰特」——水的正前方，就是滨水区；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语本土复合词：water（水，古英语 wæter）+ front（正面、朝外的一面，经由古法语来自拉丁语 frons「前额、正面」）。两半合起来就是「城镇朝水的那一面」，即滨水区。

sensesIntro.en: The senses keep the same compound in view: a strip of town facing water, first as a whole district, then as working docks, then as one property and finally as a proper name.
sensesIntro.cn: 几个义项始终不离同一条复合词：城镇朝向水的那条地带，先从整个区入手，再指作业码头，然后落到一处产业，最后用作专名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: houses with their backs to the town and their fronts to the river.
core.cn: 核心意象：房子背对城镇，正面朝着江水。

branches.en: THE TOWN: the whole district that runs along the water.
branches.cn: 城镇线：沿水展开的整个地区。

branches.en: THE PORT: wharves and warehouses make a working waterfront.
branches.cn: 港口线：码头与仓库组成作业型的滨水区。

branches.en: THE PROPERTY: a single plot that faces the water on its front.
branches.cn: 产业线：一块正面朝向水的土地。

branches.en: THE NAME: capitalized, the word becomes a street or district name.
branches.cn: 专名线：首字母大写时，这个词固定成街道或地段名。

branches.en: The district and its docks share one edge of a city turned to water.
branches.cn: 整个地区与它的码头贴着同一条边，那是城市转向水的一面。

intro.en: Waterfront is a native English compound whose second half came in through French; the parts are ordinary words rather than bound roots.
intro.cn: waterfront 是英语本土复合词，后半部分经由法语传入；两个成分都是普通词，而不是黏着词根。

latinIntro.en: Only front has a Latin ancestor, frons meaning forehead or front; Latin frons is a meaning neighbour for water, not its source.
latinIntro.cn: 只有 front 有拉丁语祖先 frons（前额、正面）；至于 water 那部分，拉丁语并没有同源词。

items.meaning: water, the element the district faces
items.meaningCN: 水；这一带所朝向的元素
items.example: The first element names what the place faces.
items.exampleCN: 第一个成分点明这一带朝向什么。

items.example: The second element gives the word its facing image.
items.exampleCN: 第二个成分提供「面朝」的意象。

items.example: Frons is the Latin ancestor of front.
items.exampleCN: frons 是 front 的拉丁语祖先。

items.example: The form -front builds many water edges.
items.exampleCN: 词形 -front 构成许多水岸词。

items.example: Riverfront swaps water for river.
items.exampleCN: riverfront 把 water 换成了 river。

items.meaning: the front of a coastal town
items.example: Seafront uses the open sea as its element.
items.exampleCN: seafront 把开阔的大海作为成分。

items.example: Beachfront names the beach edge.
items.exampleCN: beachfront 指明的是海滩边缘。

items.meaning: the water-facing edge of a town
items.example: The full compound names the edge of a town.
items.exampleCN: 整个复合词指明城镇的水边。

latinEntries.meaning: of the forehead, of the front

definition_zh: 水轮；水车；磨坊水轮；（水力驱动的）水轮装置
definition_en: a large wheel with blades or buckets that is turned by water and drives machinery such as a mill
core_image: 一只大木轮立在溪水里，水流推着叶片，轮子慢慢转起来
scene: 山间小溪旁，一座老磨坊的木轮仍在转动，水从轮上的木斗里一斗一斗倒下来。The mill has been grinding grain with a wooden waterwheel for more than a century.
sceneCN: 这里 waterwheel 是「水轮、磨坊水轮」（第 1 个义项：借水力转动、用来带动机械的大轮子）；句意是这座磨坊用一个木制水轮磨面已经超过一个世纪。画面里能辨认的物件有溪水、磨坊木轮与轮上的木斗。

pos.zh: 名词：水轮；水车；磨坊水轮（英式亦写作 water wheel）

derivatives.zh: 复合词第一部分，义为「水」，点明推动轮子的力量来源
复合词第二部分，义为「轮子」，指那只会转动的圆盘
复合形容词，义为「由水轮驱动的」，指机器靠水轮带动
由 mill 与 wheel 构成的同构复合词，义为「磨坊水轮」
由 water 与 mill 构成，义为「水力磨坊」，即安装水轮的磨坊

senses.title: A wheel driven by flowing water
senses.titleCN: 水轮：靠流水推动转动的大轮
senses.definition: a large wheel fitted with paddles or buckets that is turned by the flow of a river or stream
senses.definitionCN: 装有桨叶或木斗、借溪流水的冲力转动的大轮
senses.example: The wheelwright shaped the paddles of the waterwheel so that the stream could push them evenly.
senses.exampleCN: 轮匠把水轮的桨叶修成合适的形状，好让溪水平稳地推动它们。
senses.why: A wheel is a disc that turns on an axle, and water supplies the push, so the compound simply names the wheel that the water turns.
senses.whyCN: wheel 是装在轴上转动的圆盘，水提供推力，所以这个复合词直接点明「被水推动的轮子」。

senses.title: The wheel that powers a mill
senses.titleCN: 磨坊水轮：带动磨盘等机械的轮
senses.definition: the wheel of a water mill that converts the force of water into the turning of millstones and machinery
senses.definitionCN: 水力磨坊上的轮子，把水的力量转成磨盘与机械的转动
senses.example: Grain still travels up from the millstones, turned by an overshot waterwheel behind the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 谷物仍从磨盘处被送上来，墙后那只上射式水轮转动着它。
senses.why: Once the wheel turns, a shaft runs to the heavy stones, so the waterwheel becomes the engine of the mill itself.
senses.whyCN: 轮子一转，传动轴就通到沉重的磨盘上，于是水轮成了整座磨坊的动力机。

senses.title: A historic machine in museums and villages
senses.titleCN: 老式水力装置：磨坊、村庄里作为遗产的水轮
senses.definition: a preserved or reconstructed wheel kept as part of industrial heritage and often still working for visitors
senses.definitionCN: 作为工业遗产被保存或复原的水轮，常常还为游客现场运转
senses.example: Volunteers restored the waterwheel so that visitors could watch it turning on Sundays.
senses.exampleCN: 志愿者们复原了那只水轮，好让游客在周日看到它转动。
senses.why: Old wheels outlive the mills they drove, so the word also names the surviving machine, kept as a heritage object.
senses.whyCN: 老水轮比它所驱动的磨坊活得更久，于是这个词也指留存下来的那台机器，成为遗产物件。

senses.title: Used as a symbol of steady force
senses.titleCN: 象征：水轮比喻恒定而缓慢的推动力
senses.definition: a figurative image for a slow, steady and repeated driving force
senses.definitionCN: 比喻缓慢、恒定、反复起作用的推动力
senses.example: She compared the committee to a waterwheel, always turning and never rushing.
senses.exampleCN: 她把委员会比作水轮，不停转动却从不着急。
senses.why: The wheel turns without haste and without pause, which makes it a ready image for any steady driving force.
senses.whyCN: 水轮不急不停，自然而然成为任何恒久推动力的现成比喻。

intro.en: Waterwheel is an English compound of the native word water and the native word wheel, and the mill meaning is the oldest.
intro.cn: waterwheel 由英语本土词 water 与 wheel 组合而成，其中与磨坊相关的意思是它最古老的用法。

items.en: Water and wheel are both old native words, recorded as wæter and hweowol in Old English.
items.cn: water 与 wheel 都是古老的本土词，古英语写作 wæter 与 hweowol。

items.en: English millwrights described the turning wheel of a mill as a water wheel, in two words.
items.cn: 中古英语的磨坊匠人用两个词 water wheel 来描述磨坊里转动的轮子。

items.en: Technical writing joined the two words into one, as it did for many machine parts.
items.cn: 到十六、十七世纪，技术文献把两个词合成一个，许多机械部件的名称也是这样合并的。

items.en: Industrial handbooks classified waterwheels as undershot, breast and overshot by where the water meets the wheel.
items.cn: 十九世纪的工业手册按水流接触轮子的位置，把水轮分为下射式、胸射式与上射式。

items.en: Steam and electricity displaced the wheel as power, but heritage projects keep it turning for visitors.
items.cn: 蒸汽与电力取代了水轮的动力作用，但遗产保护项目让水轮继续为游客转动。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other compound nouns built on wheel or mill; the near-meaning group gathers machines that draw power from a flow.
note.cn: 形近组收其他由 wheel 或 mill 构成的复合名词；近义组收从流动中取得动力的机器。

entries.definition: A circular object that turns on an axle; the second half of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 装在轴上转动的圆形物体；就是这个复合词的后半部分。

entries.definition: The wheel of a mill; it names the place rather than the water that drives it.
entries.definitionCN: 磨坊的轮子；它点明所在场所，而不点明推动它的水。

entries.definition: A mill driven by water; it names the whole building rather than the wheel alone.
entries.definitionCN: 水力驱动的磨坊；指整座建筑，而不只是轮子。

entries.definition: A mill driven by wind; built on the same pattern as watermill.
entries.definitionCN: 风力驱动的磨坊；构词方式与 watermill 相同。

entries.definition: A modern wheel-like machine turned by water, steam or gas; only the idea of the turning wheel is shared.
entries.definitionCN: 被水、蒸汽或燃气推动的现代轮形机器；与水轮只共享「转动的轮子」这一观念。

entries.definition: The building that houses a waterwheel and the millstones it drives.
entries.definitionCN: 容纳水轮和它所驱动的磨盘的那座建筑。

entries.definition: The channel that carries water to the wheel and away again.
entries.definitionCN: 把水引到轮子、再把水排走的水道。

entries.definition: A gate or channel that controls the flow of water, often feeding a wheel.
entries.definitionCN: 控制水流的闸门或水道，常用来给水轮供水。

entries.definition: A wheel with flat boards that pushes against water, used on boats; the push goes the other way.
entries.definitionCN: 带平板的轮子，装在船上推水前进；受力方向正好相反。

entries.definition: Power generated from moving water, the modern successor to the wheel.
entries.definitionCN: 利用流动的水发电的动力，是水轮在现代的继任者。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two plain parts of the compound and the mill terms the wheel is found in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用这个复合词的两个普通成分，以及水轮常出现的磨坊用语。

normal.en: Water plus wheel: the wheel that the water turns.
normal.cn: water 加 wheel：被水推动转动的轮子。

normal.en: A millwheel and a waterwheel can be the same object, seen from the mill or from the river.
normal.cn: millwheel 与 waterwheel 可以是同一件东西，只是站在磨坊或站在溪边说。

normal.en: A watermill is the building, and its waterwheel is the power.
normal.cn: watermill 是那座建筑，它的 waterwheel 才是动力。

normal.en: An overshot wheel takes water over the top, while an undershot wheel is pushed at the bottom.
normal.cn: 上射式水轮让水从顶部落下，下射式水轮则在水底受推。

normal.en: Handbooks of the nineteenth century classified wheels as undershot, breast and overshot.
normal.cn: 十九世纪的手册把水轮分为下射式、胸射式与上射式。

abstract.en: Picture water tipping into buckets that carry the rim around and spill at the bottom.
abstract.cn: 想象水灌进木斗，带着轮缘转过一圈，又在底部倒回溪里。

abstract.en: Imagine the wooden axle creaking as a heavy stone begins to turn inside the mill.
abstract.cn: 想象木轴吱吱作响，磨坊里一块沉重的磨盘开始转动。

abstract.en: Think of a slow, patient turn that never stops while the stream keeps flowing.
abstract.cn: 想象只要溪水不断，轮子就一直不急不缓地转。

examples.en: The village mill still runs on a wooden waterwheel.
examples.cn: 村里的磨坊仍然靠一只木制水轮运转。

examples.en: Engineers measured the flow of the stream to size the new waterwheel.
examples.cn: 工程师测量了溪水的流量，用来确定新水轮的尺寸。

examples.en: Children watched the buckets of the waterwheel fill and empty again and again.
examples.cn: 孩子们看着水轮上的木斗一遍又一遍地灌满又倒空。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「窝特威尔」——特把水「威尔」地一推，轮子就转起来；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语本土复合词：water（水，古英语 wæter）+ wheel（轮子，古英语 hweowol）。中古英语磨坊匠人写作 water wheel 两词，后合并为 waterwheel，即「被水推动的轮子」，是水力磨坊的动力装置。

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the turning wheel itself, to the mill it drives, to the heritage object that survives the mill, and finally to the steady force it suggests.
sensesIntro.cn: 几个义项从转动的轮子本身，到它所驱动的磨坊，到磨坊消失后留存的遗产物件，最后到它所暗示的恒久推动力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a big wooden wheel standing in a stream, pushed round by the current.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只大木轮立在溪水里，被水流推着转动。

branches.en: THE WHEEL: the turning disc itself is the first and plainest sense.
branches.cn: 轮子线：转动的那只圆盘本身，是最直接也最初的义项。

branches.en: THE MILL: the same wheel turns a shaft and drives millstones.
branches.cn: 磨坊线：同一只轮子带动传动轴与磨盘。

branches.en: THE RELIC: old wheels kept after the mill closes become heritage objects.
branches.cn: 遗存线：磨坊停用后留存的老轮子，成了遗产物件。

branches.en: THE IMAGE: slow, constant turning becomes a figure for steady force.
branches.cn: 比喻线：缓慢恒定的转动变成恒定推动力的形象。

branches.en: The wheel that the water turns and the wheel that grinds the grain are one object in two roles.
branches.cn: 被水推动的轮与磨谷物的轮，是同一物件承担的两个角色。

intro.en: Waterwheel is a native English compound, and older sources often print it as two words; its parts need no prefix or suffix.
intro.cn: waterwheel 是英语本土复合词，较老的文献常把它印成两个词；它的成分既不带前缀，也不带后缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for either half; Latin rota, a wheel, is only a meaning neighbour.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词的两半都没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 rota（轮子）只是意思相近的邻词。

items.example: The first element names the power.
items.exampleCN: 第一个成分点明动力来源。

items.meaning: a disc turning on an axle
items.example: The second element names the machine part.
items.exampleCN: 第二个成分点明机械部件。

items.example: The Old English word is the ancestor of wheel.
items.exampleCN: 古英语 hweowol 是 wheel 的祖先。

items.meaning: a wheel of a certain kind
items.example: Many compound nouns end in -wheel.
items.exampleCN: 许多复合名词以 -wheel 结尾。

items.example: Millwheel names the wheel by place.
items.exampleCN: millwheel 按场所给轮子命名。

items.example: Watermill names the whole building.
items.exampleCN: watermill 指的是整座建筑。

items.example: Windmill swaps the water for wind.
items.exampleCN: windmill 把水换成了风。

items.example: The full compound names the driven wheel.
items.exampleCN: 整个复合词指明这只被驱动的轮子。

definition_zh: 网络摄像头；摄录并实时上传画面的小镜头
definition_en: a small video camera that sends live pictures to a computer or across the internet
core_image: 一枚小镜头别在电脑屏幕上方，把眼前的人与房间实时送进网络
scene: 面试前的几分钟，她对着屏幕上方的那枚小镜头整理头发，并确认画面已经传给了远端的考官。Minutes before the interview, she checked her hair in the little webcam above the screen and made sure the picture was reaching the examiner.
sceneCN: 这里 webcam 是「网络摄像头」（第 1 个义项：把画面实时送进网络的视频镜头）；句意：面试前的几分钟，她对着屏幕上方的那枚小镜头整理头发，并确认画面已经传给了远端的考官。

pos.zh: 网络摄像头；实时视频镜头

derivatives.zh: 常在网络镜头前直播的人，由 webcam 加表人的 -er 构成，属口语用法
网络直播，与 webcam 共用第一个构词成分 web，但整体来自 web 与 broadcasting 的结合
便携摄像机，与 webcam 共用 cam 这一个截短部件，但整词来自 camera 与 recorder

senses.title: A camera that streams pictures online
senses.definition: a small digital camera that sends live images to a computer or over the internet in real time
senses.definitionCN: 能把实时画面传送给电脑或由网络实时传输的小型数字摄像头
senses.example: The laptop has a webcam beside the screen, ready for video calls.
senses.exampleCN: 这台笔记本电脑屏幕旁边有一个摄像头，随时可以用来视频通话。
senses.why: The compound joins web and cam, so a camera wired to the world wide web is exactly what the name says.
senses.whyCN: 这个合成词把 web（网络）与 cam（镜头）并在一起，接上互联网络的镜头正是名字所写的东西。

senses.title: Video seen through such a camera
senses.titleCN: 摄像头画面；镜头里的影像
senses.definition: the live video image produced by such a camera, often used informally with the preposition on
senses.definitionCN: 这种摄像头拍出的实时视频画面，口语中常与介词 on 连用
senses.example: Her parents watched the graduation through the webcam on the kitchen table.
senses.exampleCN: 她的父母透过摆在厨房桌上的摄像头看完了毕业典礼。
senses.why: Because we watch an event on the camera, the device name readily shifts onto the picture it delivers.
senses.whyCN: 因为我们是「透过」摄像头看事情的，器具的名字就顺势挪到了它送出来的画面之上。

senses.title: A privacy risk of visible lenses
senses.definition: the security and privacy worry that an open lens may record or observe people without their notice
senses.definitionCN: 镜头可能在旁人不知情时录下或观看画面的安全与隐私担忧
senses.example: Many people tape over the webcam when they close the laptop.
senses.exampleCN: 许多人在合上笔记本时会用胶带把摄像头贴上。
senses.why: Any always-on lens creates a window into a room, and the word becomes shorthand for that window being open.
senses.whyCN: 任何常开的镜头都相当于给房间开了一扇小窗，于是这个词就成了「窗户开着」的同义说法。

intro.en: Webcam is a modern English blend, not an inherited older word: the clipped web and cam were joined for cameras that put their pictures on the world wide web.
intro.cn: webcam 是现代英语的截短合成，不是自古传下的旧词：web（网络）与 cam（镜头）两个截短形式拼在一起，用来指把画面送上万维网的镜头。

items.en: The clipped form webcam appears in the early 1990s for cameras that posted live pictures on the web.
items.cn: 截短形式 webcam 在二十世纪九十年代初出现，指把实时画面放到网络上的摄像头。

items.en: Web is a short form of world wide web, a named system of pages linked across the internet.
items.cn: web 是万维网名称的缩写，指通过互联网相互链接的网页系统。

items.en: Camera comes from Latin camera, a vaulted room, which entered English through camera obscura, the darkened room used by artists.
items.cn: camera 来自拉丁语 camera（拱顶房间），经由画家所用的暗室 camera obscura 进入英语。

items.en: Camera, the device for taking photographs, is first recorded in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: camera 指拍照器械的用法，文献中最早见于十九世纪。

items.en: Cam is the everyday short form of camera and is used freely in compounds.
items.cn: cam 是 camera 的日常截短形式，在合成词里被大量使用。

items.en: In current use webcam would also describe a video camera that goes to the web through an older, non-browser connection.
items.cn: 如今的用法里，经较老的非浏览器连接传上网络的视频镜头，也会被称为 webcam。

note.en: Webcam sits inside a modern family of camera and network words, and stands close to broader terms for the same device.
note.cn: webcam 处在以 camera 与网络为核心的一族现代词里，同时与泛指同类设备的几个说法相邻。

entries.definition: a broadcast sent over the web
entries.definitionCN: 播客式的网络直播节目，与 webcam 共用前面的网络成分，后面的部分来自 broadcast

entries.definition: a set of linked pages on the internet
entries.definitionCN: 网站，与 webcam 同样以网络成分开头

entries.definition: strong woven strips of fabric
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近：它来自织网、织带的古词，与互联网络无关，词源不同

entries.definition: a device for taking photographs or recording moving pictures
entries.definitionCN: 泛指照相与摄像的器械，是 webcam 的上位词

entries.definition: a meeting held by video link between distant places
entries.definitionCN: 视频会议，webcam 最常见的用途场景之一

entries.definition: a telephone that also carries pictures of the speakers
entries.definitionCN: 可视电话，功能上与视频通话相近，但指整台电话设备而非镜头

normalIntro.en: Webcam is two clipped words holding hands: web for the network and cam for the camera that feeds it.
normalIntro.cn: webcam 是两个截短词牵着手：web 指网络，cam 指把画面喂给网络的镜头。

normal.en: Cam is simply camera shortened, so webcam is a web-friendly camera with a shorter waist.
normal.cn: cam 就是 camera 的缩短形式，所以 webcam 是一个「穿短裤子」的网络镜头。

normal.en: The word is a single solid unit; do not write it as two separate words when it is one compound.
normal.cn: 这个词是一个整体，不要把它拆成两个分开的词来写，因为它是一个合成词。

normal.en: In front of a noun it describes use, as in webcam interview or webcam class.
normal.cn: 放在名词前时它描述的是用途，如 webcam interview（视频面试）与 webcam class（视频网课）。

normal.en: On webcam means with the camera switched on, which is a very frequent phrase.
normal.cn: on webcam 表示「开着摄像头」，这是一个非常高频率的说法。

normal.en: Compare camera: camera is the whole family, webcam insists on the network link.
normal.cn: 对比 camera：camera 是整族的统称，webcam 强调的是与网络的连接。

abstract.en: Picture a small glass eye clipped to the top of a laptop lid.
abstract.cn: 想象一只小小的玻璃眼睛夹在笔记本屏幕的上沿。

abstract.en: Imagine looking at a birthday cake through somebody else camera on another continent.
abstract.cn: 想象透过另一个大陆上某人的镜头，看见一块生日蛋糕。

abstract.en: See a strip of tape covering the lens, left there as a quiet warning.
abstract.cn: 想象一片胶带贴在镜头上，那是一种无声的警示。

examples.en: The online tutor asked every student to turn on the webcam.
examples.cn: 网课老师要求每位学生打开摄像头。

examples.en: She had never taken a webcam interview before, so she practised with a friend.
examples.cn: 她从未参加过视频面试，于是先和朋友演练了一遍。

examples.en: A built-in lens and a microphone mean that one device is often all you need, provided the promised picture is clear.
examples.cn: 内置镜头与麦克风意味着往往一台设备就够了，前提是它承诺的画面足够清晰。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「韦布看」——隔着网络（网）也能看清楚，靠的是头顶那枚小镜头。这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 两类现代部件合成：web（万维网的缩写，出现在二十世纪后期）+ cam（camera 的截短形式，camera 源自拉丁语 camera，拱顶房间）。二者合为 webcam，核心义「把画面送上网络的镜头」。

sensesIntro.en: Webcam names the lens first, then drifts onto the picture the lens sends, and finally onto the privacy worry that an open lens creates.
sensesIntro.cn: webcam 先指那枚镜头，再滑向镜头送出的画面，最后落到镜头常开所带来的隐私担忧上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small lens clipped to a screen, feeding live pictures into the web.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚夹在屏幕上的小镜头，把实时画面送进网络。

branches.en: The device branch names the physical camera itself.
branches.cn: 器物分支：直接指那枚实体的摄像头。

branches.en: The image branch moves from the lens to the picture it delivers.
branches.cn: 画面分支：从镜头挪到它送出来的影像。

branches.en: The risk branch turns the lens into a window someone could look through.
branches.cn: 风险分支：把镜头想象成别人可以往里看的窗口。

branches.en: Device and image are hard to separate when people talk about a live class or call.
branches.cn: 谈论直播课堂或通话时，器物与画面几乎分不开。

branches.en: Because the picture travels outward, it can also arrive where nobody intends it.
branches.cn: 正因为画面是向外传的，它也可能抵达原本无人打算让它去的地方。

intro.en: Webcam is a modern compound with no classical affix; its usable parts are the clipped web and cam, and the family words that grew around them.
intro.cn: webcam 是现代合成词，没有古典词缀；可拆解的部分是截短的 web 与 cam，以及围绕它们生成的同族词。

latinIntro.en: Only the cam element traces back to Latin camera, a vaulted room. The web element is English, so the Latin items below are background for camera rather than for the whole compound.
latinIntro.cn: 只有 cam 这一部分可以上溯到拉丁语 camera（拱顶房间）。web 是英语本族部件，所以下面的拉丁条目是 camera 的背景，而不是整个合成词的祖先。

items.example: Web is the short form of world wide web.
items.exampleCN: web 是万维网名称的缩写。

items.example: Cam is the everyday short form of camera.
items.exampleCN: cam 是 camera 的日常截短形式。

items.example: Webcam joins the network and the lens in one word.
items.exampleCN: webcam 用一个词把网络与镜头连在一起。

items.example: The suffix -s makes the plural webcams.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -s 构成复数 webcams。

items.example: Webcast shows the same web prefix at work.
items.exampleCN: webcast 展示了同样的网络前缀的用法。

items.example: Website shares the web part with webcam.
items.exampleCN: website 与 webcam 共用网络这个部分。

items.example: The suffix -er forms the informal webcammer.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成口语词 webcammer。

items.example: Camcorder borrows the cam shortening again.
items.exampleCN: camcorder 再次借用了 cam 这个截短形式。

items.meaning: a person who often appears on a webcam
items.example: Webcammer is informal and not used in exams.
items.exampleCN: webcammer 属口语，考试中很少用。

latinEntries.meaning: dark chamber, the source of the English word for camera
latinEntries.meaningCN: 暗室，英语 camera 一义的直接来源

definition_zh: 楔子；楔形物；把……楔住；使挤入
definition_en: a piece of wood or metal that is thick at one end and thin at the other, driven in to split or hold something
core_image: 一块一头厚一头薄的木块被敲进缝隙，硬生生把两边撑开
scene: 木匠把一块厚头薄刃的木块对准木桩顶上的裂缝，抡起锤子把它一路砸了下去。The carpenter aimed a block of wood at the crack in the log and hammered the wedge in deeper with each blow.
sceneCN: 这里 wedge 是「楔子」（第 1 个义项：一头厚一头薄、用来撑开或固定东西的小块）；句意：木匠把一块厚头薄刃的木块对准木桩顶上的裂缝，抡起锤子把它一路砸了下去。

pos.zh: 楔子；楔形物；鞋楔；三角三明治

collocations.zh: 用楔子抵住门（不让关上）

derivatives.zh: 被卡住的；被夹紧的，由过去分词转作形容词
楔形的；呈楔状的，由 wedge 加形容词后缀 -y 构成
楔形的；呈尖角状的，用连字符由 wedge 与 shape 合成

senses.title: A piece that splits or holds
senses.definition: a block of wood, metal, or another hard material, thick at one end and tapering to a thin edge, driven in to split or fasten
senses.definitionCN: 一端厚、另一端逐渐变薄、用于劈开或固定的木块、金属块等硬物
senses.example: He hammered a wooden wedge into the log to split it.
senses.exampleCN: 他把一块木楔砸进木桩，将其劈开。
senses.why: The Old English word meant a tool you knock into a gap, and the new split widens because the thin edge enters first and the thick end follows.
senses.whyCN: 古英语里的这个词指敲进缝隙的工具：薄刃先进、厚头随后，缝隙就被越撑越开。

senses.title: A triangle that has been cut away
senses.definition: a solid piece of something cut or shaped like a wedge, such as a slice of cake or cheese
senses.definitionCN: 形状像楔子的固体块，如一块蛋糕或奶酪
senses.example: She saved me a wedge of lemon with the tea.
senses.exampleCN: 她给我留了一块柠檬配茶。
senses.why: Once the tool shape is familiar, any cut piece with one wide side and one sharp point is called a wedge by resemblance.
senses.whyCN: 工具的形状一旦被人熟悉，任何一边宽、一边尖的切块都会因形似而被称为 wedge。

senses.title: Something driven in to divide people
senses.definition: a force or act that pushes two sides apart, especially one that breaks up a relationship
senses.definitionCN: 把两方推开的力或行为，尤指破坏关系的挑拨
senses.example: Gossip drove a wedge between the two sisters.
senses.exampleCN: 流言在姐妹俩之间插了一刀。
senses.why: The physical wedge splits wood in two, so the abstract sense borrows the picture of two halves forced apart.
senses.whyCN: 实物的楔子把木头劈成两半，抽象的义项就借用了这个被硬掰开的画面。

senses.title: A pointed formation of a group or shape
senses.definition: a shape or group arranged with a narrow leading point and a wide rear, such as birds flying in a vee
senses.definitionCN: 前端尖、后方宽的队形或形状，如排成人字形的飞鸟
senses.example: The geese flew over the lake in a wedge.
senses.exampleCN: 一群大雁排成楔形飞过湖面。
senses.why: The shape of the tool, with its point forward, is applied to formations pressed through the air or onto a field.
senses.whyCN: 工具前端尖的形状被搬到穿透空气或场地的队形上。

senses.title: To force in or fix with a wedge
senses.definition: to push something with effort into a narrow space, or to use a wedge to keep it in place
senses.definitionCN: 用力把某物塞进狭窄空间，或用楔子把它固定住
senses.example: The case was wedged behind the wardrobe, so we could not reach it.
senses.exampleCN: 箱子卡在衣柜后面，我们根本够不着。
senses.why: The ordinary case of using the tool became the verb for any firm pushing of one thing into another.
senses.whyCN: 使用这个工具最常见的做法变成了动词，泛指把一件东西牢牢塞进另一件东西里。

intro.en: Wedge comes from Old English wecg, with cognates across the Germanic languages; the modern spelling settled only in the later Middle English and early modern period.
intro.cn: wedge 来自古英语 wecg，在日耳曼诸语中都有同源词；现代拼写到中古英语后期甚至近代早期才固定下来。

items.en: A reconstructed form such as wagjaz, a thing of triangular shape, is the usual starting point for this Germanic word.
items.cn: 这个词在日耳曼语中的起点通常被勾勒为重构形式 wagjaz，意为呈三角形的物件。

items.en: Old English wecg names the splitting tool, and the word is also used for a lump or a mass.
items.cn: 古英语 wecg 指劈开木头所用的工具，也用来指一块、一团。

items.en: Spellings such as wegge and wege compete before the form with d settles.
items.cn: 中古英语里有 wegge、wege 等多种拼写相互竞争，最后才定了带 d 的写法。

items.en: Wedge moves from the workshop into metaphor, and the idea of driving a wedge between two parties becomes current.
items.cn: wedge 从工坊走进比喻，表示在双方之间打进一个楔子的说法开始通行。

items.en: Golf clubs, shoe inserts, and slices of food all borrow the triangle, and a group in pointed formation is a wedge too.
items.cn: 高尔夫球杆、鞋垫和食物切块都借用了三角形，排成尖头队形的人群也叫 wedge。

note.en: Wedge names both a splitting tool and the shape it leaves, and it stands close to other words about forcing things into gaps or splitting them apart.
note.cn: wedge 既指劈开东西的工具，也指它形成的形状，并与「塞进缝隙」和「劈开」这两类词相邻。

entries.definition: a row of bushes forming a barrier or boundary
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近：它来自栅栏与树篱的古词，与楔子无关，词源不同

entries.definition: a tall grass that grows in wet ground
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近：它是湿地禾草的旧名，与楔子无关，词源不同

entries.definition: a narrow flat shelf, especially on a cliff or wall
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近：它指墙上或崖壁突出的窄台，与楔子无关，词源不同

entries.definition: a block used to stop something from rolling or sliding
entries.definitionCN: 轮挡、垫块，用来挡住会滑动的物体，功能与楔子接近但形状更方

entries.definition: a thin piece of material used to fill a small gap
entries.definitionCN: 薄垫片，用来填平细微缝隙，作用与楔子相似但更薄

entries.definition: to split something or break apart along its lines
entries.definitionCN: 劈开，指把东西顺纹理分成两半，是楔子最常用来完成动作

normalIntro.en: Wedge is a very short, very solid word, and it behaves like the object it names: it squeezes into tight places.
normalIntro.cn: wedge 这个短词本身就很敦实，用起它来也像它所指的物件：总往狭窄处里挤。

normal.en: Wedge-shaped is the adjective for anything with one thick end and one thin edge.
normal.cn: wedge-shaped 形容任何一头厚、一边薄的物件。

normal.en: Drive a wedge between means break up a relationship, the most common figurative use.
normal.cn: drive a wedge between 意为破坏关系，是它最常见的比喻用法。

normal.en: As a verb the word quietly takes the -s plural and past form wedged, spelled with a single d after the g.
normal.cn: 作动词时，它的复数与过去式写为 wedges、wedged，g 后面只带一个 d。

normal.en: A wedge of something points at food: a slice of cheese, cake, or fruit cut with a wide back and a point.
normal.cn: a wedge of something 多指食物，如厚背尖头的一块奶酪、蛋糕或水果。

normal.en: Compare wedgy: the adjective is rarer in exams, so use wedge-shaped when you describe a shape.
normal.cn: 对比 wedgy：这个形容词在考试中较少见，描述形状时多用 wedge-shaped。

abstract.en: Picture the pointer of a clock face turned into a block of wood, thick at the middle and sharp at the tip.
abstract.cn: 想象表盘上的指针变成一块木头，中间厚、尖端利。

abstract.en: See a slice of lemon resting on the rim of a glass.
abstract.cn: 想象一片柠檬搁在玻璃杯的杯沿上，宽的一头朝外。

abstract.en: Hear an argument pushed in like a nail between two people sitting side by side.
abstract.cn: 想象一句挑起争端的话像钉子一样，被钉进并排坐着的两个人之间。

examples.en: The musician placed a wedge in the gap to hold the lectern steady.
examples.cn: 乐手在缝隙里塞了块楔子，把谱架固定住。

examples.en: Her coat was wedged between the seats and took a while to pull free.
examples.cn: 她的外套夹在座位之间，费了好一会儿才拽出来。

examples.en: Careless words can drive a wedge between neighbours who used to share everything.
examples.cn: 不经意的话语会在原本什么都共用的邻里之间插进一道裂痕。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吾皆」——两半都被我分开，靠的就是那块厚头薄刃的小木块。这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 重构的日耳曼语形式 wagjaz（三角形之物）→ 古英语 wecg（楔子；一块）→ 中古英语 wegge、wege 等拼写竞争 → 近代英语 wedge，核心义「薄刃插入、厚头撑开的三角块」。

sensesIntro.en: Wedge begins with the splitting tool, extends by shape to slices and to formations, borrows the force of splitting for metaphors of dividing people, and ends as a verb for forcing things into tight spaces.
sensesIntro.cn: wedge 从劈开东西的工具出发，按形状扩展到三角切块与队形，借用「劈开」的力表达离间，最后作动词表示把东西硬塞进狭窄处。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick-backed block with a thin edge, driven into a gap until the gap opens.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块背厚刃薄的木块被敲进缝隙，直到缝隙被撑开。

branches.en: The tool branch is where the word starts.
branches.cn: 工具分支：这是词的本源。

branches.en: The shape branch treats any triangle slice as a small relative of the tool.
branches.cn: 形状分支：任何三角形切块都被当作工具的小亲戚。

branches.en: The dividing branch carries the splitting force into human relations.
branches.cn: 离间分支：把劈开的力带进了人与人的关系。

branches.en: The formation branch puts the pointed shape into the air or onto the field.
branches.cn: 队形分支：把尖头形状放进空中或场地。

branches.en: The verb branch names the pushing itself, tool or no tool.
branches.cn: 动词分支：直接命名「塞进去」这个动作，有没有工具都行。

intro.en: Wedge is a short Germanic root word with almost no affixation of its own; its family comes from the plural -es, the adjective -y, and the past form -ed.
intro.cn: wedge 是一个简短的日耳曼语词根词，本身几乎没有词缀；它的词族靠复数 -es、形容词后缀 -y 与过去式 -ed 形成。

latinIntro.en: Wedge has no Latin ancestry: its root is Germanic. The Latin words below are near meanings and background for the splitting tool, not ancestors of the word.
latinIntro.cn: wedge 没有拉丁语来源，它的词根属日耳曼语。下面的拉丁词只作近义与背景对照，不是这个词的祖先。

items.example: Wecg is the Old English shape of the word.
items.exampleCN: wecg 是这个词的古英语形态。

items.example: Wedge keeps the noun sense alive today.
items.exampleCN: wedge 至今仍是名词。

items.example: The suffix -es forms the plural wedges.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -es 构成复数 wedges。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms the past wedged.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成过去式 wedged。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms the participle wedging.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成现在分词 wedging。

items.meaningCN: 具有……性质的形容词词尾
items.example: The suffix -y forms the rare adjective wedgy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成少用的形容词 wedgy。

items.meaning: having the form of a wedge
items.example: Wedge-shaped joins the noun to shape with a hyphen.
items.exampleCN: wedge-shaped 用连字符把名词与 shape（形状）连起来。

items.meaning: stuck fast in a narrow space
items.example: Wedged describes a thing that cannot move.
items.exampleCN: wedged 形容被卡得动不了的东西。

items.example: Wedgy is rare and mostly literary.
items.exampleCN: wedgy 少见，多用于文字描写。

latinEntries.meaning: a wedge-shaped body part in anatomy
latinEntries.meaningCN: 解剖学上楔形的结构（仅作语义对照）

definition_zh: 小麦；小麦的麦粒；小麦植株
definition_en: a cereal plant grown for its grain, which is ground into flour for bread and other foods
core_image: 一片金黄的麦田在风里起伏，每根麦穗都压弯了腰
scene: 祖父站在地头，抓起一把刚收获的麦粒，说这一季的收成全看春天有没有下透雨。Standing at the edge of the field, my grandfather took a handful of the wheat just harvested and said the whole crop depended on the spring rain.
sceneCN: 这里 wheat 是「小麦」（第 1 个义项：磨成面粉做面包的麦类作物）；句意：祖父站在地头，抓起一把刚收获的麦粒，说这一季的收成全看春天有没有下透雨。

collocations.phrase: separate the wheat from the chaff

derivatives.zh: 小麦制的；麦粉做的，由 wheat 加形容词后缀 -en 构成
麦田，由 wheat 加 field 合成
小麦草，由 wheat 加 grass 合成，常指榨汁饮用的嫩苗

senses.title: A cereal plant grown for its grain
senses.definition: a cereal plant with long dense heads of grain, grown widely in temperate regions and milled into flour
senses.definitionCN: 一种温带地区广泛种植、穗长而密的谷物，通常磨成面粉
senses.example: Wheat is one of the oldest crops people still grow.
senses.exampleCN: 小麦是人们至今仍在种植的最古老的作物之一。
senses.why: The Old English word named the grain-bearing plant itself, and English kept the mass-noun plant name for the crop in the field.
senses.whyCN: 古英语中的这个词本指结籽的植株本身，英语保留了这个集体名词义，用来指田里的作物。

senses.title: The grain that is milled
senses.definition: the small hard seeds of this plant, used as food and ground into flour
senses.definitionCN: 这种植物结出的坚硬小籽粒，可作食物并磨成面粉
senses.example: The mill grinds wheat into fine flour for bakers.
senses.exampleCN: 磨坊把小麦磨成细面粉供面包师使用。
senses.why: Since the grain is what gets harvested and traded, the same word naturally also means the seeds rather than the plant.
senses.whyCN: 因为真正被收割、被交易的是麦粒，同一个词就自然同时指籽粒而非植株。

senses.title: What is worth keeping after screening
senses.definition: a valued part or substance left after unwanted things are separated from it, as in a proverb about grain and husks
senses.definitionCN: 去掉杂物后留下的有价值部分，常出现在「分清谷物与糠壳」的谚语里
senses.example: Judging entries carefully separates the wheat from the chaff.
senses.exampleCN: 仔细评判参赛作品，才能把好的与差的分开。
senses.why: Farmers winnow grain from husks, and the picture of solid seed beside weightless chaff became a metaphor for separating value from dross.
senses.whyCN: 农民把谷物与糠壳扬开，实心籽粒旁边是轻飘飘的碎壳，这个画面成了「分清好坏、存良去劣」的比喻。

intro.en: Wheat goes back to Old English hwaete, whose unrecorded earlier form began with a hw cluster that became a plain wh sound in modern English.
intro.cn: wheat 可上溯到古英语 hwaete，其更早形式未能直接记录，开头是 hw 这样的音节簇，在现代英语中演变为 wh 的读法。

items.en: A form such as hwaitijaz is reconstructed as the common Germanic ancestor; this part is reconstruction, not a written record.
items.cn: 这部分的共同语祖语形式如 hwaitijaz 属重构，并非文献记录。

items.en: Danish hvede and German Weizen both descend from the same source, showing a Germanic origin rather than a Latin one.
items.cn: 丹麦语 hvede 与德语 Weizen 同出这一来源，说明它的祖源是日耳曼语而非拉丁语。

items.en: Old English hwaete names the cereal, and related words describe the pale white colour of its flour.
items.cn: 古英语 hwaete 指这种谷物，与之相关的词描写其面粉的灰白色调。

items.en: Spellings shift towards whete as the hw sound settles into wh, and the grain keeps feeding the staple bread supply.
items.cn: 随着 hw 演变为 wh，拼写逐渐转向 whete，这种谷物一直是主食面包的来源。

items.en: Proverbs and metaphors grow from farming: separating valuables from worthlessness is pictured through grain and chaff.
items.cn: 农耕中长出了谚语与比喻：用谷物与糠壳的画面来形容分辨价值与无用之物。

items.en: Wheat now stands for the mass noun in trade, in whole wheat bread, and in global food policy, where prices and yields are debated.
items.cn: 今天的 wheat 在贸易、全麦面包与全球粮食政策的讨论中，都是不可数的集体名词。

note.en: Wheat belongs to the cereal field of words, and it is often learned beside other grains and kinds of flour.
note.cn: wheat 属于谷物义场，学习中常与其它粮食及面粉类词一起记。

entries.definition: a cereal grass with bearded grain used for flour, beer, and animal feed
entries.definitionCN: 大麦，同为禾本科谷物，常与小麦放在一起背，但并非同源

entries.definition: a cereal plant grown for its grain in cool climates
entries.definitionCN: 燕麦，同属谷物，常与小麦对比生长条件

entries.definition: a small thrush with white on the tail
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近：它是麦穗鹟，鸟名，词源与小麦无关，纯属巧合

entries.definition: the seeds of cereals used as food, or any cereal plant
entries.definitionCN: 谷物、粮食的通称，是 wheat 的上位词

entries.definition: any grassy plant grown for its edible seeds
entries.definitionCN: 谷类作物，涵盖小麦、大麦、燕麦等的类称

entries.definition: the main cereal crop of a region, maize in North America
entries.definitionCN: 指某地的主要谷物，北美常指玉米；与小麦的对应关系因地区而变

normalIntro.en: Wheat is a short noun whose shape is plain, so the family words are the best hook: wheaten, wheatfield, wheatgrass.
normalIntro.cn: wheat 拼写朴素，记住它最省力的勾子是它的同族词：wheaten、wheatfield、wheatgrass。

normal.en: Whole wheat on a label means the flour uses the whole grain, husk and all.
normal.cn: 包装上写 whole wheat，意味着面粉用了整粒麦子，连麸皮一起。

normal.en: Wheat flour is the everyday link between the crop and the bread on the table.
normal.cn: wheat flour 把田里的作物和桌上的面包直接连在一起。

normal.en: Keep the wheat from the chaff is a common idea for sorting good from bad.
normal.cn: 分清谷物与糠壳，是英语里常用来表达「存良去劣」的意象。

normal.en: The noun is usually uncountable, so say some wheat or a kilo of wheat, not a wheat.
normal.cn: 这个词通常不可数，说 some wheat 或 a kilo of wheat，不说 a wheat。

normal.en: Compare grain and cereal: they are wider words, wheat names one particular plant.
normal.cn: 对比 grain 与 cereal：这两个是更宽泛的词，wheat 则特指某一种作物。

abstract.en: See a field of golden stalks bent over with heavy heads.
abstract.cn: 想象一片金黄的麦秆被沉甸甸的麦穗压弯。

abstract.en: Watch a mill turn small hard seeds into a cloud of fine flour.
abstract.cn: 想象一座磨坊把坚硬的小籽粒磨成一团细粉。

abstract.en: Hold two things in your hands, one heavy and one weightless, and blow the light one away.
abstract.cn: 两手分别握着一样沉的东西和一样轻的东西，一吹，轻的飞走了。

examples.en: Farmers in this region grow wheat and barley side by side.
examples.cn: 这个地区的农民把小麦和大麦种在一起。

examples.en: Rising temperatures may cut wheat yields in dry areas.
examples.cn: 气温上升可能降低干旱地区的小麦产量。

examples.en: The school lunch programme now uses local wheat flour for its bread.
examples.cn: 学校的午餐计划现在用本地的小麦面粉做面包。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂他」——用最朴素的小麦粉喂饱一家人，正是庄稼最实在的用处。这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 重构的日耳曼语形式 hwaitijaz（一般认为与「白色」有关，指面粉的颜色）→ 古英语 hwaete → 中古英语 whete → 英语 wheat，核心义「一片金黄、磨粉做面包的谷物」。

sensesIntro.en: Wheat starts as the plant in the field, moves naturally to the grain that is harvested and milled, and then rises above farming into a metaphor for separating value from waste.
sensesIntro.cn: wheat 先是田里的植株，顺势转到被收割、被磨碎的麦粒，最后跳出农事，成为分辨价值与废料的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wave of golden stalks bent by heavy heads of grain.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片金黄的麦秆被沉甸甸的麦穗压得起伏。

branches.en: The crop branch keeps the plant in the field, in the growing season.
branches.cn: 作物分支：留住田里、生长季里的植株。

branches.en: The grain branch shifts to the seed, the thing actually stored and sold.
branches.cn: 麦粒分支：转向真正被储存、被出售的籽粒。

branches.en: The metaphor branch lifts winnowing out of the barn into judgement about people and things.
branches.cn: 比喻分支：把扬场的动作搬出谷仓，用于对人的判断与取舍。

branches.en: Plant and grain share the picture, which is why a farm report may mix the crop with the price of grain.
branches.cn: 植株与籽粒共用同一幅画面，所以农业报道会把作物与粮价放在一起说。

branches.en: Only the heaviest, most substantial grain survives the winnowing, which is the point of the metaphor.
branches.cn: 扬场之后只剩下最实在、最有分量的籽粒，这正是比喻的意思所在。

intro.en: Wheat is a plain Germanic noun with almost no affix, but it forms a small, useful family with -en, with compounds such as wheatfield, and with the plural -s.
intro.cn: wheat 是朴素的日耳曼语名词，本身几乎没有词缀，但靠着 -en、wheatfield 这类合成以及复数 -s，长成了一个实用的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Wheat has no Latin ancestry; its root is Germanic. The Latin words below are background for grain crops and bread making, not ancestors of the word.
latinIntro.cn: wheat 没有拉丁语来源，词根属日耳曼语。下面的拉丁词是谷物与制面包的背景语汇，并非这个词的祖先。

items.example: Hwaete is the recorded Old English form.
items.exampleCN: hwaete 是有记录的古英语形式。

items.meaning: the cereal plant or its grain
items.example: Wheat is normally used as an uncountable noun.
items.exampleCN: wheat 通常作不可数名词使用。

items.example: The suffix -s forms the plural wheats, used for kinds of grain.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -s 构成复数 wheats，多指多种小麦。

items.example: The suffix -en forms the adjective wheaten.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -en 构成形容词 wheaten。

items.example: Wheaten describes old-fashioned bread made of wheat.
items.exampleCN: wheaten 常形容用小麦做的老式面包。

items.example: Wheatfield joins the crop to the field.
items.exampleCN: wheatfield 把作物与田地连在一起。

items.meaning: the young shoots of wheat, often juiced
items.example: Wheatgrass joins the crop to grass.
items.exampleCN: wheatgrass 把作物与草连在一起。

items.example: Chaff sits opposite wheat in the proverb.
items.exampleCN: 在谚语里 chaff 与 wheat 相对。

items.example: Whole wheat appears on almost every bakery label.
items.exampleCN: whole wheat 几乎出现在每家面包店的标签上。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 斯佩耳特小麦或粗磨谷物（仅作语义对照）

definition_zh: 有益健康的；身心健康的；品德端正的；风气良好的
definition_en: good for the health and well-being of body or mind, or improving and morally sound
core_image: 一碗热气腾腾的全谷粥：完整、干净、能养人
scene: 奶奶端来一碗热气腾腾的燕麦粥，里面只有完整谷粒和新鲜的苹果块。Grandma set down a bowl of steaming oats, which she called a wholesome breakfast that would keep me warm all morning.
sceneCN: 这里 wholesome 是「有益健康的」（第 1 个义项：对身体或身心有益的食物）；句意：奶奶端来一碗热气腾腾的燕麦粥，说这是一顿有益健康的早餐，能让我暖和一整个上午。图片可辨识的物件：土陶碗、燕麦粥、苹果块与餐巾。

pos.zh: 有益健康的；身心健康的
品德端正的；风气良好的

derivatives.zh: wholesome + -ness，义为「健康有益的性质；端正」
un- + wholesome，义为「不健康的；有害身心的」
whole + sale 复合词，义为「批发的；大规模的」
whole + -ness，义为「完整；圆满」

senses.title: Good for the body
senses.definition: food or drink that is clean, nourishing and good for the body
senses.definitionCN: 干净、有营养、对身体有益的食物或饮料
senses.example: A wholesome breakfast of oats and fruit gives children a good start.
senses.exampleCN: 一顿由燕麦和水果组成的健康早餐能让孩子有个好开始。
senses.why: Wholesome is whole plus -some: something that is whole and undamaged is taken to be sound for the body.
senses.whyCN: wholesome 是 whole 加后缀 -some，意为「保持完整、没有损伤的」，完整的东西被看成对身体有益的东西，于是长出「健康」这一核心义。

senses.title: Good for the mind
senses.definition: activities, surroundings or habits that keep the mind and mood in good health
senses.definitionCN: 能让心理与情绪保持健康的活动、环境或习惯
senses.example: Long walks in the hills became a wholesome habit for the whole family.
senses.exampleCN: 在山间长途散步成了全家人的健康习惯。
senses.why: The sense spreads from food to whatever keeps a person whole inside, so fresh air, exercise and good company also count.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项从食物扩展到一切让人内在保持完整健全的事物，所以新鲜空气、运动与好伙伴也算 wholesome。

senses.title: Morally sound
senses.titleCN: 品德端正的；风气良好的
senses.definition: interests, shows or behaviour that are proper, clean and morally good
senses.definitionCN: 正当、干净、符合道德的兴趣、节目或行为
senses.example: The magazine promises wholesome entertainment for young readers.
senses.exampleCN: 这本杂志承诺为年轻读者提供健康向上的娱乐。
senses.why: The older moral sense comes through -some in its old meaning of having the characteristics of; wholesome meant having the nature of what is good.
senses.whyCN: 古老的道德义来自 -some 的旧义「具有……性质的」：wholesome 原指「具有良善本性的」，所以引申为「端正、不低俗」。

senses.title: Mildly moralistic in tone
senses.titleCN: 显得一本正经的；说教味的
senses.definition: used in a slightly mocking way about things that are too safe, dull or goody-goody
senses.definitionCN: 略带调侃地形容过于安全、无趣或一本正经的东西
senses.example: Critics called the new cartoon a wholesome but dull piece of work.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家称这部新动画片健康却乏味。
senses.why: When wholesomeness hardens into a label, it can look cautious and slow, so the word shades into a faint put-down.
senses.whyCN: 当「健康」被固化成标签，它就带上小心翼翼、缺乏刺激的味道，于是这个词飘出一丝贬义。

senses.title: Sound and healthy in an old sense
senses.definition: an older use for a body that is sound, unharmed and free from disease
senses.definitionCN: 较早的用法，指身体健全、未受损伤、没有疾病
senses.example: In old texts a wholesome body meant a body free of disease.
senses.exampleCN: 在古文本里，wholesome body 指的是没有疾病的健全身体。
senses.why: The oldest sense sits closest to whole: a whole body is an unhurt one, and unhurt became healthy.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项离 whole 最近：完整的身体就是没有受损的身体，而「未受损」进一步变成「健康的」。

intro.en: Wholesome joins the Old English word for whole, hal, with the suffix -some, from an old word of unknown origin meaning having the nature of.
intro.cn: wholesome 由古英语表示「完整、健康」的 hal 与后缀 -some 组合而成；这个后缀源出一个来源不确定的旧词，意为「具有……性质的」。

items.en: Hal meant whole, healthy and sound; it is the ancestor of modern whole and also of heal.
items.cn: 古英语 hal 意为完整的、健康的、健全的，是今天 whole 的前身，heal 也出自这里。

items.en: Halsum is already recorded in the twelfth century with the idea of health-giving.
items.cn: halsum 早在十二世纪就有记载，已带「能带来健康」的意思。

items.en: The suffix -some always meant having a certain quality, as in buxom or lithe; halsum meant of sound nature.
items.cn: 后缀 -some 一直表示「具有某种性质」，如 buxom、lithe；halsum 意为「本性健全的」。

items.en: The spelling moves from halsum toward wholesome as the long o is written with wh.
items.cn: 随着长元音逐渐写作 wh 开头的拼法，拼写从 halsum 过渡到 wholesome。

items.en: The moral sense grows at the same time: something wholesome is good in nature and fit to be given to children.
items.cn: 道德义同时发展起来：wholesome 的东西本性良善，适合给孩子。

items.en: Today wholesome covers food, habits, entertainment and an environment, often with a faint air of propriety.
items.cn: 今天 wholesome 可修饰食物、习惯、娱乐与环境，常带一点「一本正经」的口气。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words sharing whole and the suffix -some; the near-meaning group gathers words that also mean good for you or proper.
note.cn: 形近组收共享 whole 与后缀 -some 的词族；近义组收同样表示「有益」或「正当」的词。

entries.definition: Entirely, completely, built on whole plus -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「完全地、整个地」，由 whole 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: A word made with the same -some suffix and an older root meaning to bend.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「丰满健美的」；构词上与本词共用 -some 后缀，但词根是古英语「弯曲」，只是构词方式相同。

entries.definition: Tasty, literally pleasing to the tooth, made with the same -some suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「美味的」，字面是「宜牙的」，与 wholesome 共用 -some 后缀。

entries.definition: Good for the body; the plainest everyday word for the food sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「健康的、有益健康的」，是「食物」义项最日常的说法。

entries.definition: Rich in the nutrients the body needs; focused on food value only.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有营养的」，只强调食物中营养成分的价值。

entries.definition: Correct and acceptable in a moral or social sense, close to the moral sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「正当的、得体的」，接近 wholesome 的道德与规矩义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real whole root, the -some suffix and the phrases the word keeps today.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记法基于真实的 whole 词根、-some 后缀，以及这个词今天保留的固定搭配。

normal.en: Wholesome sets whole beside some: something that makes you more whole, not less, is wholesome.
normal.cn: wholesome 里写着 whole 加 some：让你更完整而不是更残缺的东西，就是 wholesome。

normal.en: Whole and heal share the old root hal, so at the heart of wholesome is the idea of being healed.
normal.cn: whole 与 heal 同出古英语 hal，所以 wholesome 的核心是「被治好、恢复健全」。

normal.en: The suffix -some marks a quality, as in handsome and troublesome, so wholesome means full of wholeness.
normal.cn: 后缀 -some 表示某种性质，如 handsome、troublesome，因此 wholesome 就是「充满健全」的。

normal.en: Remember the fixed pairs: wholesome food, wholesome entertainment and a wholesome atmosphere.
normal.cn: 记住几组固定搭配：wholesome food、wholesome entertainment 与 wholesome atmosphere。

normal.en: The negative is made with un-, not with no-, so say unwholesome water or an unwholesome climate.
normal.cn: 否定形式用 un- 而不是 no-，应该说 unwholesome water 或者 unwholesome climate。

abstract.en: Picture a steaming bowl of oats with apple pieces, untouched by sugar or packets.
abstract.cn: 想象一碗冒着热气的燕麦粥，里面是苹果块，没有糖也没有包装袋。

abstract.en: Think of a country lane where children run while the evening air smells clean.
abstract.cn: 想象一条乡间小路，孩子们在里面奔跑，傍晚的空气中带着干净的草木味。

abstract.en: Imagine a film the whole family can watch together, with nothing to explain away afterwards.
abstract.cn: 想象一部全家可以一起看的电影，看完之后不需要向孩子解释什么奇怪的内容。

examples.en: Wholesome meals cooked at home often cost less than fast food.
examples.cn: 在家做的健康饭菜往往比快餐更便宜。

examples.en: Parents asked for more wholesome activities in the school holiday programme.
examples.cn: 家长们要求在学校的假期活动中安排更多有益身心的项目。

examples.en: The town kept its wholesome image, with clean streets and friendly shops.
examples.cn: 这座小镇保持着风气良好的形象，街道干净，店铺友善。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「厚润生」——厚实又滋润、能生养身体的，就是有益健康；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 hal（完整、健全，今天 whole 的前身）+ -some（具有……性质的）→ halsum → wholesome；核心义「完整而健全」→ 「有益健康」→ 「端正良好」。

sensesIntro.en: Wholesome starts from a whole and sound body, spreads to whatever keeps body and mind healthy, then to good conduct, with a faint mocking sense at the edge.
sensesIntro.cn: wholesome 从「完整的、健全的身体」出发，扩展到一切让身心保持健康的事物，再到端正的品行，最后边缘处衍生出略带调侃的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a simple bowl of whole oats, clean and warm, feeding a sound body.
core.cn: 核心意象：一碗朴素的整粒燕麦粥，干净、温热，滋养健全的身体。

branches.en: Food that keeps the body whole and strong is the first everyday sense.
branches.cn: 让身体保持完整强健的食物，是第一个日常义项。

branches.en: Once food becomes habits and surroundings, wholesomeness covers the mind.
branches.cn: 一旦从食物扩展到习惯与环境，令人受益的范围就延伸到心理层面。

branches.en: Good conduct is the moral branch, where wholeness becomes decency.
branches.cn: 端正品行是道德分支，在这里「完整」变成了「干净正派」。

branches.en: The mocking edge appears when a good label feels too safe and dull.
branches.cn: 当「健康」的标签显得过分安全乏味时，就出现了调侃的边缘义。

branches.en: The oldest sense of an unhurt body is the seed from which the health sense grew.
branches.cn: 「身体完好」这一最古的义项，正是「健康」义生长出来的种子。

intro.en: Wholesome is built from an Old English root plus the suffix -some; English then makes wholesomeness, unwholesome and the whole family.
intro.cn: wholesome 由古英语词根加后缀 -some 构成，英语再围绕它造出 wholesomeness、unwholesome 与整个词族。

latinIntro.en: The word has no Latin source, but the whole root is distantly related through Proto-Germanic heal to Latin salus, health and safety.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源；但其整体词根经由原始日耳曼语的「健康」一路可远溯到拉丁语 salus（健康、安全）。

items.example: Hal is the Old English root behind whole and heal.
items.exampleCN: hal 是 whole 与 heal 背后的古英语词根。

items.meaningCN: 本性健全的；能带来健康的
items.example: Halsum is the twelfth-century ancestor of the modern word.
items.exampleCN: halsum 是这个词十二世纪的前身。

items.example: The suffix -some marks a quality, as in handsome.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -some 表示某种性质，如 handsome。

items.example: Whole is the living base word of wholesome.
items.exampleCN: whole 是 wholesome 的现用基础词。

items.meaning: to make or become healthy again
items.example: Heal shares the same old root as whole.
items.exampleCN: heal 与 whole 同出一个古老词根。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms wholesomeness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 wholesomeness。

items.meaning: the quality of being good for you
items.example: Wholesomeness names the quality itself.
items.exampleCN: wholesomeness 指这种性质本身。

items.example: The prefix un- forms unwholesome.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unwholesome。

items.meaning: bad for the body or mind
items.example: Unwholesome describes what harms health.
items.exampleCN: unwholesome 描述损害健康的东西。

items.meaning: in a healthy or proper way
items.example: Wholesomely is a rare but valid adverb.
items.exampleCN: wholesomely 少见但确实存在的副词。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 安全的；未受损的；健全的

definition_zh: 野生动植物；野生生物；（总称）野生动物
definition_en: animals and plants that live and grow freely in nature, without being kept or planted by people
core_image: 林间小径旁突然窜过的鹿：没人喂养，也没人牵绳
scene: 清早沿着湖边小径散步，一只鹿从灌木里探出头来张望。On my dawn walk by the lake, a deer stepped out of the bushes and stood still, as if the wildlife owned the path.
sceneCN: 这里 wildlife 是「野生动植物」（第 1 个义项：在自然中自由生存、无人饲养或栽种的动植物）；句意：在湖边破晓散步时，一只鹿从灌木中走出来站定，仿佛这条小路归野生生灵所有。图片可辨识的物件：湖面薄雾、木栈小径、灌木与鹿角剪影。

pos.zh: 野生动植物；野生生物（总称，不可数）

forms.label: 不可数名词，无复数形式
作定语用（置于另一名词前）

derivatives.zh: wildlife + -er，口语指「野生动物保护工作者」
复合词前半，义为「野生的；未驯化的」
wild + -ness，义为「野性；荒凉」

senses.title: Animals and plants living freely in nature
senses.definition: the animals and plants that live without human care in forests, fields, rivers and seas
senses.definitionCN: 在森林、田野、河流与海洋中不受人类照料而生存的动物与植物
senses.example: The wetland is home to rare birds and other wildlife.
senses.exampleCN: 这片湿地是珍稀鸟类和其它野生动植物的家园。
senses.why: The word is simply wild joined to life, so it names the whole living world that is not tame, farmed or planted.
senses.whyCN: 这个词就是 wild 与 life 的复合：它指整个没有被驯化、饲养或栽种的活着的世界，所以是「野生动植物」的总称。

senses.title: Wild animals seen in a place
senses.definition: the wild creatures that live in one particular area, counted one by one
senses.definitionCN: 生活在某一特定区域的野生动物，可以一个一个地数
senses.example: The valley supports a rich variety of wildlife, from otters to eagles.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷养育了丰富的野生动物，从水獭到老鹰都有。
senses.why: Conservation and tourism slowly narrowed the broad sense to the animals of one place, because those are the creatures visitors come to see.
senses.whyCN: 保护与旅游语境把这个宽泛的词慢慢收窄到「某地的动物」，因为游客专程来看的就是这些动物。

senses.title: Related travel and media use
senses.definition: used before another noun in wildlife film, wildlife photographer or wildlife tourism
senses.definitionCN: 用于 wildlife film、wildlife photographer、wildlife tourism 等复合名词之前
senses.example: She works as a wildlife photographer in northern Canada.
senses.exampleCN: 她在加拿大北部做野生动物摄影师。
senses.why: Once people go looking for wild creatures, the word turns into a label for films, trips and jobs built around them.
senses.whyCN: 人一旦为看野生生物而出发，这个词就变成一种标签，用来修饰围绕它们拍的片子、走的旅程和从事的职业。

senses.title: Protected status
senses.definition: creatures that the law protects from hunting, capture or trade
senses.definitionCN: 受法律保护、禁止猎捕或买卖的生物
senses.example: Under the new law, wildlife in the park may not be caught or sold.
senses.exampleCN: 根据新法律，园内的野生生物不得被捕捉或出售。
senses.why: The word often carries a duty: because wildlife belongs to no one, the law steps in as its keeper.
senses.whyCN: 这个词常带一份责任：正因为野生生物不属于任何人，法律才出面充当它们的守护者。

intro.en: Wildlife is an English compound, not a borrowed word: it puts the old adjective wild together with the noun life.
intro.cn: wildlife 是英语自己的复合词，并非外来借词：它把古老的形容词 wild 与名词 life 拼在一起。

items.en: Wilde meant living in a natural state and not tamed or controlled by people.
items.cn: 古英语 wilde 意为「处在自然状态、未被驯化或控制的」。

items.en: Lif meant life, and also a way of living or a body; both halves are native English.
items.cn: 古英语 lif 意为生命，也指生活方式或活着的身体；两半都是英语本族词。

items.en: Writers begin to use wild life, first as two words, to mean animals not kept by people.
items.cn: 十九世纪的作家开始使用 wild life（最初写作两个词），指不被人饲养的动物。

items.en: The two words are joined as wildlife, and the word becomes standard in game laws and nature writing.
items.cn: 两个词合并写作 wildlife，并在狩猎法规与自然写作中成为标准用词。

items.en: After the conservation movement, wildlife covers plants as well, and gives rise to wildlife film, wildlife reserve and wildlife tourism.
items.cn: 保护运动兴起之后，wildlife 也涵盖植物，并派生出 wildlife film、wildlife reserve、wildlife tourism 等复合词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds that share one half of wildlife; the near-meaning group separates wildlife from fauna, flora and other nature words.
note.cn: 形近组收与 wildlife 共用一半构件的复合词；近义组把 wildlife 与 fauna、flora 等自然类词区分开。

entries.definition: A wild, uncultivated area; it shares the wild root but names a place, not creatures.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「荒野、未开垦之地」；与 wildlife 共用 wild 词根，但指的是地方而不是生物。

entries.definition: A fire spreading freely through countryside, made with the same wild.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「野火」，由同一个 wild 构成，但后半是 fire 而非 life。

entries.definition: The period a person or thing lives, made with the same life.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一生、寿命」，与 wildlife 共用 life 这一部分。

entries.definition: The animals of a region, taken as a group; a scientific word with no plants.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「（某地区的）动物群」，属科学用语，不含植物。

entries.definition: Any living animal, often one at a time rather than as a group.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「生物、动物」，常指单独一个个体，而不是整体。

entries.definition: Farm animals kept for use; the opposite of wild in everyday farming language.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「家畜」，即为人饲养利用的动物，与「野生」相对。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two real halves of the compound, wild and life, and the phrases the word keeps today.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记法基于这个复合词真实的两半 wild 与 life，以及这个词今天保留的搭配。

normal.en: Wildlife is wild plus life, so read it as the life that stays wild.
normal.cn: wildlife 就是 wild 加 life，可以直接读成「仍然野着的那部分生命」。

normal.en: It is uncountable: say much wildlife or plenty of wildlife, never many wildlifes.
normal.cn: 它不可数：说 much wildlife 或 plenty of wildlife，不要说 many wildlifes。

normal.en: The half life also appears in lifetime and lifestyle, all built the same English way.
normal.cn: 后半 life 也出现在 lifetime 和 lifestyle 里，都是同样的英语复合方式。

normal.en: Wilderness is the place where wildlife lives, wild plus ness names the land, wild plus life names the creatures.
normal.cn: wilderness 是野生动物生活的地方：wild 加 ness 指土地，wild 加 life 指生物。

normal.en: Remember the fixed pairs: wildlife conservation, wildlife reserve and a wildlife documentary.
normal.cn: 记住固定搭配：wildlife conservation、wildlife reserve 与 wildlife documentary。

abstract.en: Imagine a deer coming out of the bushes at dawn while the path is still empty of people.
abstract.cn: 想象天刚亮时一只鹿从灌木里走出，而小径上还没有人。

abstract.en: Picture a fox, a heron and a spray of reeds sharing one river bank.
abstract.cn: 想象一只狐狸、一只苍鹭和一片芦苇共享同一条河岸。

abstract.en: See a photographer kneeling in grass for hours, waiting for a single bird to lift its head.
abstract.cn: 想象一位摄影师在草丛里跪了几个小时，只为等一只鸟抬头。

examples.en: The new road cut through the forest and disturbed the local wildlife.
examples.cn: 新修的公路穿过森林，惊扰了当地的野生动物。

examples.en: Volunteers counted the wildlife in the marsh to check the health of the wetland.
examples.cn: 志愿者们统计沼泽中的野生生物，以判断湿地的健康状况。

examples.en: People are asked to keep their distance and let the wildlife stay wild.
examples.cn: 人们被要求保持距离，让野生动物保持野性。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歪尔莱夫」——歪着头、在野外过自己的日子，谁也别想牵回家，那就是野生的生命；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语形容词 wild（古英语 wilde，野生的、未驯化的）+ life（古英语 lif，生命）→ 复合名词 wildlife；核心义「不靠人饲养或栽种的活物」，再收窄为「某地的野生动物」与「受保护生物」。

sensesIntro.en: Wildlife begins as a broad noun for all living things left wild, narrows to the animals of one place, and grows into a label for films, trips and protected species.
sensesIntro.cn: wildlife 起初泛指一切保持野生状态的活物，随后收窄为某地的野生动物，再发展为影片、旅程的题材标签与受保护物种的称呼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a deer stepping onto a forest path with no fence and no owner.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只鹿踏上林间小径，没有围栏，也没有主人。

branches.en: The broad total of free living things is the starting sense.
branches.cn: 一切自由生存的活物，是这个词最基本的义项。

branches.en: Counted place by place, the same noun narrows to local animals.
branches.cn: 按地方逐个来数时，同一个词就收窄为当地的野生动物。

branches.en: Films, photographers and tourism turn the noun into an attributive label.
branches.cn: 影片、摄影师与旅游业把这个名词推到定语位置，形成题材标签。

branches.en: Legal protection adds the sense of creatures that belong to no one and so need a keeper.
branches.cn: 法律保护又添一层：这些生物不属于任何人，因此需要看守者。

branches.en: The total and the local list are the same word used at different scales.
branches.cn: 「总和」与「局部清单」其实是同一个词在不同尺度上的用法。

intro.en: Wildlife is a native English compound of two free words, so its family grows by compounding rather than by affixation.
intro.cn: wildlife 由两个独立的英语本族词复合而成，因此它的词族主要靠复合构词，而不是靠加词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin has no word for wildlife as such; the closest are fauna, the animals of a region, and fera, wild beasts.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语没有与 wildlife 完全对应的词，最接近的是 fauna（某地区的动物群）与 fera（野兽）。

items.example: Wild is the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: wild 是这个复合词的前半。

items.meaning: the state of being alive, living things
items.example: Life is the second half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: life 是这个复合词的后半。

items.example: With -ness, wild makes wilderness, the untamed land.
items.exampleCN: wild 加 -ness 构成 wilderness，即未驯化的土地。

items.example: Wilderness names the place, not the creatures.
items.exampleCN: wilderness 指地方，不指生物。

items.example: Wildfire pairs wild with fire instead of life.
items.exampleCN: wildfire 把 wild 与 fire 配对，而不是 life。

items.example: Wildfowl is another old compound with wild.
items.exampleCN: wildfowl 是另一个含 wild 的老复合词。

items.example: Lifestyle pairs life with style the same way.
items.exampleCN: lifestyle 用同样的方式把 life 与 style 组合。

items.example: Lifetime is built from life plus time.
items.exampleCN: lifetime 由 life 加 time 构成。

items.example: Wildlife conservation is its commonest partner word.
items.exampleCN: wildlife conservation 是它最常见的搭配。

definition_zh: 柳树；柳木；垂柳；柳木制品
definition_en: a tree with long thin branches that hang down and narrow leaves, or the wood of this tree
core_image: 河岸边一棵垂柳：细长的枝条整片垂下来，随水风摆
scene: 清早沿河散步，一排枝条很长、一直垂到水面的树把小路遮成了绿廊。At dawn the riverside path came alive with birdsong, and a willow beside the bridge drooped its pale green strands toward the water.
sceneCN: 这里 willow 是「柳树」（第 1 个义项：枝条细长下垂、喜生于水边的树）；句意：破晓时分，河岸的小路在鸟鸣中醒来，桥边一棵柳树把它淡绿的枝条垂向水面。图片可辨识的物件：河岸石阶、下垂的枝条、水面倒影与远处小桥。

derivatives.zh: willow + -y，字面为「多柳的」，多用来形容人身材细高柔美
willow + ware，义为「绘有柳树图案的瓷器」

senses.title: The tree with drooping branches
senses.definition: a tree that grows near water and has long thin branches that hang down
senses.definitionCN: 生长在水边、枝条细长下垂的树
senses.example: Willows line both banks of the slow river.
senses.exampleCN: 柳树成排立在缓流的河两岸。
senses.why: The name comes from an Old English tree word, and the drooping shape of its branches is what most people picture.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字来自古英语的树名，而枝条整片垂下的形状正是大多数人想起柳树时的画面。

senses.title: The wood of the tree
senses.definition: the light, flexible wood of this tree, used for baskets and small tools
senses.definitionCN: 这种树浅色而柔韧的木材，用于编篮与制作小工具
senses.example: The basket was woven from willow cut in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这个篮子是用冬天砍下的柳条编成的。
senses.why: The flexible branches made the wood useful for weaving, so the tree name also came to mean its material.
senses.whyCN: 柔韧的枝条让这种木材特别适合编织，于是树名也引申为木材本身。

senses.title: Willow as a symbol
senses.definition: a tree used in art and tradition as a sign of grief, parting or spring
senses.definitionCN: 在艺术与传统中用作哀愁、离别或春天象征的树
senses.example: In many folk songs the willow stands for a farewell by the water.
senses.exampleCN: 在许多民歌里，柳树代表水边的离别。
senses.why: The bending branches and riverside habit give the tree a mood, so cultures use it for sorrow and for parting.
senses.whyCN: 弯曲的枝条与临水而生的习性给这棵树带来一种情调，于是各种文化用它表达哀愁与离别。

senses.title: Willow in craft and medicine
senses.definition: objects woven from willow, or willow bark, a source of salicin used against pain and fever
senses.definitionCN: 用柳条编成的器物，或柳树皮（含柳苷，用于镇痛退热）
senses.example: Many people once chewed willow bark to ease a fever.
senses.exampleCN: 过去很多人咀嚼柳树皮来退烧。
senses.why: Because the tree gives both baskets and medicine, the word appears in craft names and in the history of pharmacy.
senses.whyCN: 这棵树既能给篮子原料又能入药，所以这个词既出现在工艺名称里，也出现在药学史里。

senses.title: Plants or objects named after it
senses.titleCN: 以柳命名的植物或物件
senses.definition: other plants and things that recall the willow, such as willow herb or willow pattern
senses.definitionCN: 其它让人联想到柳树的植物或事物，如柳兰、柳纹瓷
senses.example: The willow warbler is a small bird that sings from willow twigs.
senses.exampleCN: 柳莺是一种常在柳枝间鸣唱的小鸟。
senses.why: A familiar tree becomes a measuring stick, and people name birds, flowers and patterns after it.
senses.whyCN: 一种熟悉的树成了参照物，人们就用它的名字去命名鸟、花与图案。

intro.en: Willow comes from Old English welig, a native Germanic tree name, with the final shape of the modern word settled later.
intro.cn: willow 来自古英语 welig，是一个日耳曼语系的土生树名；现代拼写在后来才定型。

items.en: Welig names the willow in early English writing.
items.cn: 古英语 welig 是早期英语文献中对柳树的称呼。

items.en: Related words in other Germanic languages, such as Dutch wilg and Old Saxon wilgia, show a common origin.
items.cn: 荷兰语 wilg 与古撒克逊语 wilgia 等亲属语言中的同源词表明有共同来源。

items.en: The word grows an extra ending, written wylow or wilow, under the influence of similar tree words.
items.cn: 受其它树名的影响，这个词多了一个词尾，写作 wylow 或 wilow。

items.en: The spelling is fixed as willow, and the plural willows becomes ordinary.
items.cn: 拼写被固定为 willow，复数 willows 也成了常用形式。

items.en: The adjective willowy develops from much willow into slender and graceful.
items.cn: 形容词 willowy 由「柳树茂密的」发展出「身材细长柔美的」意思。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on or near the tree name; the near-meaning group gathers trees and plants people confuse with the willow.
note.cn: 形近组收由这个树名派生的词与拼写易混词；近义组收容易和柳树混淆的树木与植物。

entries.definition: A tall plant with pink flowers whose seed pods look like willow leaves.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「柳叶菜」，开粉色花，果荚形似柳叶，与 willow 构成复合词。

entries.definition: Gracefully slender, like the thin flexible branches of the tree.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「（身材）细长柔美的」，像柳树细而柔韧的枝条。

entries.definition: Something to rest your head on; it rhymes with willow but has a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「枕头」；与 willow 押韵，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A tall fast-growing tree often planted along roads, with upright leaves.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「杨树」，高大速生，常种在路旁，叶子多直立。

entries.definition: A slender tree with white bark, often planted in northern parks.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「桦树」，树干细长、树皮发白，北方公园常见。

entries.definition: A kind of willow grown for basket making, a specialist word for the same plant.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「杞柳、编筐柳」，是同一种植物的专门说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English tree name and the compounds the word forms today.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记法基于真实的古英语树名，以及这个词今天组成的复合词。

normal.en: Willow begins with will, so picture a tree that bends to the wind because it wills itself to be soft.
normal.cn: willow 开头是 will，可以想象一棵自愿把腰弯向风里的树，因为它很软。

normal.en: The word rhymes with pillow, and willow branches hang down like a pillow resting on the water.
normal.cn: 这个词与 pillow 押韵，柳枝垂下来正像一只搁在水面上的枕头。

normal.en: Weeping willow uses the old image of bending branches as tears.
normal.cn: weeping willow（垂柳）沿用了「弯垂的枝条正如眼泪」这一旧的比喻。

normal.en: Willow bark contains salicin, the natural cousin of aspirin, so the tree carries a small history of medicine.
normal.cn: 柳树皮含柳苷，是阿司匹林的天然近亲，所以这棵树本身带着一小段医学史。

normal.en: Willowy means slender and graceful, never simply made of wood.
normal.cn: 派生词 willowy 意思是「身材细长柔美的」，并不只是指「用柳木做的」。

abstract.en: Picture long thin branches hanging like curtains into a slow green river.
abstract.cn: 想象细长的枝条像帘子一样垂进碧绿缓慢的河水里。

abstract.en: Imagine weaving a winter-cut willow twig into the rim of a basket.
abstract.cn: 想象把冬天砍下的柳条一圈一圈编进篮子的边沿。

abstract.en: See a lone willow on a bank in a folk song, where people say goodbye to the ferry.
abstract.cn: 民歌里想象岸边一棵孤零零的柳树，人们就在那里向渡船告别。

examples.en: Farmers planted willows along the ditch to hold the soil in place.
examples.cn: 农民沿沟种下柳树，以固定土壤。

examples.en: The old willow tree by the mill has stood for more than a hundred years.
examples.cn: 磨坊旁那棵老柳树已经站立了一百多年。

examples.en: She wove a willow basket for the spring market.
examples.cn: 她为春天的集市编了一个柳条篮子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「微罗」——微风轻罗，柳条垂下来摇摇摆摆，像轻薄的丝罗一样晃；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 welig（柳树）→ 中古英语 wylow / wilow → 英语 willow；同源词见于荷兰语 wilg 等日耳曼语。核心义「枝条细长下垂的临水树」，再引申为「柳木」「柳制品」与「绵绵情思的象征」。

sensesIntro.en: Willow begins as the name of a tree, and spreads to its wood, its use in craft and medicine, and its place as a symbol of parting.
sensesIntro.cn: willow 先是某种树的名字，随后扩展到它的木材、在编织与医药中的用途，以及作为离别象征的形象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a riverside tree with long strands of branches hanging into the water.
core.cn: 核心意象：河岸边一棵挂着长长下垂枝条、一直伸进水里的树。

branches.en: The tree and its wood are the physical starting point of the word.
branches.cn: 树本身与它的木材，是这个词的实体起点。

branches.en: From the tree comes the material, its light and bendable wood.
branches.cn: 由树得到材料，也就是这种浅色可弯曲的木材。

branches.en: Craft and medicine both turn the tree into useful things, one cut and woven, one boiled and chewed.
branches.cn: 编织与药用都把树变成有用的东西：一个切成条再编，一个煮水或咀嚼。

branches.en: The familiar tree also lends its name to other plants and objects.
branches.cn: 这种熟悉的树还把自己的名字借给其它植物与器物。

branches.en: The bender of branches and the tree of farewell in song share one soft, yielding image.
branches.cn: 被枝条压弯的树与歌里那棵送别的树，共享同一种柔顺低垂的形象。

intro.en: Willow is a single native tree name, so its small family grows by the suffixes -y and -ware and by compounding.
intro.cn: willow 是一个完整的本族树名，它的词族很小，靠后缀 -y、-ware 与复合方式扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin name for the willow is salix, the root of words like salicin, the painkilling compound found in its bark.
latinIntro.cn: 柳树的拉丁学名是 salix，也是 salicin（柳苷，柳树皮中的镇痛成分）等词的词根。

items.example: Welig is the earliest English form of the tree name.
items.exampleCN: welig 是这个树名最早的英语形式。

items.example: Willow is the modern form of the old tree name.
items.exampleCN: willow 是这个古老树名的现代形式。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -y forms willowy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成 willowy。

items.example: Willowy moves from many willows to a graceful figure.
items.exampleCN: willowy 从「柳树多的」变成形容身形优雅。

items.example: Weeping forms weeping willow, the common park tree.
items.exampleCN: weeping 构成 weeping willow，即公园常见的垂柳。

items.example: Willowware pairs the tree with ware.
items.exampleCN: willowware 把这棵树与 ware（器物）组合。

items.example: Osier is a French loan for a willow used in baskets.
items.exampleCN: osier 是从法语借来的词，指用来编筐的柳树。

items.example: Withe names a willow twig twisted into a band.
items.exampleCN: withe 指盘成箍圈的柳条。

items.meaning: the painkilling compound in willow bark
items.meaningCN: 柳苷（柳树皮中的镇痛成分）
items.example: Salicin is named after Latin salix, the willow.
items.exampleCN: salicin 得名于拉丁语 salix，即柳树。

latinEntries.meaning: the painkilling compound found in willow bark
latinEntries.meaningCN: 柳苷（柳树皮中的镇痛成分）

definition_zh: 意志力；毅力；自制力
definition_en: the mental strength that lets you control your own behaviour and keep trying towards a goal
core_image: 疲惫的手仍紧按开关，不让身体先放弃
scene: 冬夜的书桌前，考生反复合上又打开书。Late at night, it took real willpower to keep studying instead of going to bed.
sceneCN: 这里 willpower 是「意志力」（第 1 个义项：控制自己、坚持目标的精神力量）；句意：深夜时分，他靠真正的意志力才坚持继续学习，而不是上床睡觉。

derivatives.zh: will 加 -ful 构成，意为「任性的；故意的」
will 加 -ing 构成，意为「愿意的」
复合词加 -ed，意为「靠意志驱动的」

senses.title: Mental strength to control yourself
senses.definition: the strength of mind to control your own actions and resist temptation
senses.definitionCN: 控制自身行为、抵抗诱惑的心智力量
senses.example: It took willpower to refuse the second slice of cake.
senses.exampleCN: 忍住不吃第二块蛋糕需要意志力。
senses.why: Will names the faculty of choosing, and power names force, so the compound says the force of choosing is strong enough to hold.
senses.whyCN: will 指做选择的官能，power 指力量，两者合起来就是「能够把握住自己的选择之力」。

senses.title: Strength to keep going
senses.definition: the determination to continue a difficult effort until the goal is reached
senses.definitionCN: 坚持一项艰难努力直到达成目标的决心
senses.example: Her willpower carried her through four months of training.
senses.exampleCN: 她的毅力支撑她完成了四个月的训练。
senses.why: The same inward force also pushes forward in time, so the word extends from resisting temptation to persisting in work.
senses.whyCN: 同一股内在力量还会在时间上向前推动，因此该词从「抵抗诱惑」延伸到「坚持不懈」。

senses.title: Willpower as an effortful resource
senses.titleCN: 作为有限资源的意志力
senses.definition: the amount of mental effort a person can spend on self control before becoming tired
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在疲劳之前可用于自我控制的心力总量
senses.example: Decisions late in the day drain your willpower.
senses.exampleCN: 一天中较晚做出的决定会消耗你的意志力。
senses.why: If willpower is a force that can be spent, it can also be measured, exhausted and restored, as psychologists now say.
senses.whyCN: 既然意志力是一种会被消耗的力量，它就能被测量、用尽与恢复，这正是现代心理学中该词所指的意义。

intro.en: Willpower joins the native English word will with power, a noun borrowed from Old French, and the compound is recorded from the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: willpower 由英语本族词 will（意志）与借自古法语的 power（力量）合成，一般认为十九世纪才见诸记录。

items.en: Willa means the mind, desire, or choice, from a Germanic root.
items.cn: 古英语 willa 指心意、欲望或选择，源于日耳曼语词根。

items.en: Poeir, from Latin posse, means to be able.
items.cn: 古法语 poeir（源出拉丁语 posse）意为能够做到。

items.en: Power enters English and names strength or ability to act.
items.cn: power 进入英语，指行事的力量或能力。

items.en: The compound willpower appears in discussion of self control and character.
items.cn: 大约十九世纪，合成词 willpower 出现在关于自制与品格的论述中。

items.en: Psychology treats willpower as a limited resource for self regulation.
items.cn: 现代心理学把意志力看作自我调节的一种有限资源。

items.en: Everyday English uses willpower for sport, dieting and study habits.
items.cn: 日常英语把该词用于运动、节食与学习习惯等语境。

note.en: Willpower is a compound of will and power, close to willingness and willful in form, and to self control and grit in meaning.
note.cn: willpower 是 will 与 power 的合成词，形式上与 willingness、willful 同族，意义上与自制力、坚韧相近。

entries.definition: the quality of being ready to do something
entries.definitionCN: 愿意；情愿

entries.definition: done on purpose or showing stubborn determination
entries.definitionCN: 故意的；任性的

entries.definition: the ability to control your own impulses
entries.definitionCN: 自制；自控

entries.definition: firmness of purpose in reaching a goal
entries.definitionCN: 决心；坚定

entries.definition: courage and resolve shown over a long period
entries.definitionCN: 坚韧；毅力

entries.definition: training and control of conduct
entries.definitionCN: 纪律；自律
